item.title: Gemini app hits 1 billion monthly users, Google teases what’s next
item.description:
Source: 9to5Google Score: 6.88
Google today announced that over 1 billion people are using the Gemini app every month. CEO Sundar Pichai announced the milestone, with Gemini being Google’s “fastest growing product ever.” It is the company’s 14th product to hit that milestone along with Search, Gmail, Android, Maps, Chrome, Play, and YouTube. In May of 2025, Google reported 400 million monthly active users. A year later that figure hit 900 million, and Google noted another 50 million by late July. Meanwhile, Gemini app vice president Josh Woodward shared what Google has learned “from the first billion, and what’s coming next.” Over a tenth of those users (100+ million) are on iOS, with power users on the macOS app prompting approximately “2x more frequently than other surfaces.” As previewed at I/O 2026 in May, the Gemini app is “rolling out 60+ new regional dialects soon” (timestamped below). Additionally, ”63% of users now talk directly to Gemini,” with the executive noting how there are “more ‘voice only’ users.” With Gemini Live, 1 in 5 interactions “go beyond voice” to leverage live camera and screen sharing. Gemini is responsible for generating over 150 million images per day, while the app is adding more study features “over the next few weeks.” On the Android front, Google highlighted task automation across 40 apps, with “more updates coming tomorrow” at Made by Google 2026. More on Gemini: - Gemini will create mobile & desktop apps in the future as AI Studio for Android, iOS is canceled - Gemini Spark can now use Chrome to auto browse, AI Pro access goes international - Gemini for macOS rolling out voice control and Gboard Rambler-level transcription Comments

item.title: Ask Maps in Google Maps rolling out Personal Intelligence, real-time transit, global launch
item.description:
Source: 9to5Google Score: 6.28
After rolling out in March, the Gemini-powered Ask Maps chat in Google Maps is getting a number of big updates today, including a global launch. After the US launch, Ask Maps — find it underneath the search bar — is rolling out in English to “Australia, Brazil, Canada, Indonesia, Japan, and Mexico, along with over 150 countries and territories.” Ask Maps can now tap into Personal Intelligence, like the Gemini app and AI Mode. The first integration is Gmail, with Ask Maps now able to factor “your upcoming flight or dinner reservations, giving you relevant suggestions without you having to explain your existing plans.” For example, if you’re traveling, try asking: “Give me ideas on how to spend a few hours near the hotel before my flight tomorrow.” You’ll see nearby recommendations based on your hotel reservation in Gmail — along with tips for getting to the airport afterwards, like what time to leave. You have to manually enable Personal Intelligence in Ask Maps, with support for Google Calendar and other apps coming soon. Meanwhile, Ask Maps now remembers past conversations to easily continue them if History settings are enabled. Simply ask, “Remind me, what activities did you suggest for my trip to Seattle?” Maps will instantly pull up your previous ideas so you don’t have to start planning from scratch. In addition to traffic, Ask Maps can now tap into real-time transit information for buses, trains, subways, and ferries: “Is there a ferry to get to Taronga Zoo with views of the Opera House?” This “virtual departure board” in the chat will update in real time if there are any delays. These three features are rolling out “everywhere Ask Maps is available.” New agentic capabilities allow Ask Maps to accomplish complex, multi-step tasks, like ordering food. An example prompt is “order spicy pad kee mao with seafood for me to pick up on my way home” (from work). Google will find open restaurants along your route, factor in saved places, and account for dietary needs. After you select a place, Ask Maps will place the required dish in your cart for you to finalize. Ask Maps supports Square and Toast at launch, with Uber Eats support “coming soon.” There’s also support for booking hotels (with Ask Maps comparing prices and availability) and finding local events. “For next week’s conference in downtown Miami, find me a decently priced, top-rated hotel with an artsy vibe, within walking distance from a gym and restaurants. Ask Maps in the Contribute tab now lets you conversationally suggest edits, like “more parking is available behind the building.” You can even upload a photo of a storefront sign — Maps will detect the new hours from the image, and ask you to confirm before submitting the suggestion for you. Food ordering, hotel and event discovery, and conversational contributions are rolling out now in the US. Comments

item.title: New Gemini overlay for Wear OS rolling out to Pixel Watch
item.description:
Source: 9to5Google Score: 5.55
Gemini on Wear OS is getting a new overlay design that takes after Neural Expressive on Android phones to boost cross-device consistency. Previously, activating Gemini on Wear OS would open the full app. This new overlay appears over your current watch face, similar to Android phones and tablets. It features Gemini’s Neural Expressive background, as well as the spark icon and greeting. Screenshots on the Play Store show a transcript of your prompt and action confirmations. A small tweak moves the system microphone privacy indicator from the bottom of your screen to the top. The full Gemini app on Wear OS also features the visual updates, thus unifying the assistant across all platforms. Google does not appear to have made any changes to Gemini responses. This redesign was first previewed in May and on the Samsung Galaxy Watch 9. Gemini Intelligence on Wear OS lets you use task automation on upcoming watches. Version 1.36 of Google Gemini on Wear OS has widely rolled out via the Play Store, but this new look has a server-side component that’s not yet widely available. More on Gemini: - Gemini will create mobile & desktop apps in the future - Gemini Spark can now use Chrome to auto browse, AI Pro access goes international - Gemini for macOS rolling out voice control and Gboard Rambler-level transcription Comments

item.title: What new Google Messages features are rolling out [August 2026]
item.description:
Source: 9to5Google Score: 5.51
Like other Google apps, Messages for Android A/B tests many features. It can take the RCS/SMS client a rather long time to actually launch new functionality in stable. From various reports, Google announcements, and devices we’ve checked, this is the current state of Messages. Update 8/8: Still rolling out (beta) These are Messages features that Google announced or have been spotted in the wild by beta users. [New] Customizable attachments grid [Updated] Long-press menu Instead of a top toolbar, long-pressing on a message or image opens a floating menu as the background blurs. Another press lets you copy just a part of the chat. Previously, you had to copy the entire message. Chat theme Google Messages is letting you more extensively customize conversations with “Chat theme.” Replacing “Change colors” from 2024, you can access this new option from the three-dot overflow menu. Be on the lookout for a red badge when this is rolled out for your phone. The Colors carousel themes message bubbles. There are nine options, with Dynamic Color being the first option and responding to the background of your chat. Your other eight options are static, like before. The Wallpapers option lets you change the background of the conversation. In addition to uploading your own image, Google provides the following collections: Animals, Architecture, Black & White, Cityscapes, Landscapes, Macro, Space, Sunsets, and Textures. iOS 27 adds replies & photo reactions to Android-iPhone RCS When iOS 27 launches this fall, Android-iPhone conversations over RCS will gain support for inline replies that include quotes, as well as photo reactions with the actual emoji instead of just the text description. This feature is currently in beta. Read receipts redesign II In recent weeks, Google Messages has mostly reverted to the two-circle read receipts underneath the message design after trying a single circle within the bubble. Google is now testing a variant that uses the old icons but moves the timestamp and encryption lock. You now view that information by swiping left, with direct replies accessed by a right swipe. Messages for web removing QR code pairing Going forward, Messages for web users will have to use Google Account sign-in. As of late April, the QR code method is still available. Read receipts redesign I Read receipts are now placed in a circle at the bottom-right corner of message bubbles and images. You swipe left to see timestamps and the encryption lock, while you can swipe right to reply. This first started appearing in August of 2024, but is now seeing wide beta and stable availability. | Ellipsis | Sending | | Single check with ring | Sent | | Double check with ring | Delivered | | Double check solid circle | Read | Recent launches (stable) Samsung Messages discontinued In the US, Samsung is having users switch to Google Messages. On Android 14+, Google’s RCS app will “automatically shift” to your homescreen dock after the move. Bolder voice message button Google now themes the voice message button with a bolder color after previously having the waveform match the compose field Top comment by twylight Jfc what is so hard about adding categories for conversations? Old vs. new Tap to draft This new option helps reduce accidental Smart Replies. After enabling in Settings > Suggestions & Actions > Suggestions, tapping a Smart Reply will place it in the text field to allow for further edits before you manually tap the Send button. “Tap to send” remains available and is the default behavior. - Selfie GIF consistently appears - Encrypted RCS for Android and iPhone with iOS 26.5 - Trash folder - Real-time location sharing - @mentions in group RCS chats - Gemini-powered Scam Detection - Edit History in Details page - Toned down Nano Banana Remix - Camera tweaks - Bigger Gemini FAB - Link preview redesign - Leave unknown group chats - Image viewer redesign - Remix with Nano Banana - Tweaked camera + gallery icon - Account menu redesign - Spam link detection - Key Verifier - Standalone gallery - Material 3 Expressive redesign - Sensitive Content Warnings - Details page redesign - Custom group chat icons - Delete for everyone - Snooze notifications - RCS status in updated ‘New chat’ contacts list - Gallery + camera redesign with ‘Original quality’ sending - Expanded text field limit - Real-time and expanded Scam Detection - Unsubscribe for SMS and RCS spam - Double tap to thumbs up - Text field redesign 2025 - Improved media receiving performance - Custom profile pictures - ‘Your profile’ name and photo settings - “Magic Rewrite” button - Camera face filters - Gemini double FAB - RCS message editing - Group search in new conversations screen - Full RCS Messages transfer on Pixel 9 - RCS photo with text caption redesign - New “Select recipients” conversation picker - Show expressive animations - Larger contact photos - Voice recorder redesign with noise cancellation + Voice Moods - Single-line text field - Selfie GIF - Custom Bubbles and backgrounds - Profiles - Reaction Effects - Revamped Contact Details page - Photomoji - Magic Compose - Google Account Device pairing Comments

item.title: Google Home update adds support for viewing third-party cameras from Wyze, Eufy, more
item.description:
Source: 9to5Google Score: 5.43
While hit-or-miss support has been in place for years, Google Home’s latest update supposedly brings better support for third-party camera brands, including the likes of Wyze, Anker’s Eufy, and more. The ability to use all of your smart home gear in a single place is one of the best aspects of the Google Home app, but it’s only a half-measure for cameras. While countless third-party brands have long supported Google Home integration for smart displays, proper live viewing in the Home app has been very hit-or-miss. Cameras from Arlo have offered support for some time, and there was also a point where cameras from Reolink and TP-Link (Tapo) showed up – though functionality is very inconsistent. Some Wyze cameras also work well in Google Home. This week, Google says that “a wider range of cameras” now support viewing “home security feeds” in the Google Home app alongside cameras from Nest and Walmart. Supported brands include: - Eufy (by Anker) - Tapo (by TP-Link) - Wyze - Reolink - Nanit Support for more camera brands: You can now connect a wider range of cameras, including those from Eufy, Tapo, Wyze, Reolink & Nanit, and view all your home security feeds in one place inside the Google Home app. You’ll notice that a few of those have already been supported in some capacity over the years, but it sounds like Google is perhaps opening the door to proper support. Hopefully, that means some performance improvements. If you’re using any of these camera brands, let us know in the comments if they’re working better. The rest of the latest Google Home update includes a new “Save clip” button for event recordings from Nest & Walmart cameras and several other quality-of-life improvements. Google explains: - New quick ‘Save Clip’ shortcut: New shortcut makes it easier to download event recordings straight from your camera view. Just tap the 3-dot menu next to any recording in your event list to save it instantly by clicking on the download shortcut. (Tip: Want a custom clip length? Use the menu button while playing or scrolling the timeline!). - AI event descriptions (Home Premium Advanced): Subscribers can now read helpful, auto-generated event summaries right inside the full-screen camera view so you know what happened at a glance. - Smarter camera view defaults: The main camera view now opens directly to your timeline or event list so you can jump straight to important moments. - Auto full-screen in landscape: Rotate your phone sideways while watching a live feed or recording in portrait to automatically jump into full-screen view. - Longer live streaming: Watch your Nest camera live streams for longer without interruptions, thanks to under-the-hood stability improvements. - Quick stream reconnects (Android): If your Wi-Fi or cellular connection drops, the app instantly notices and gives you a quick retry button to get your live view back up fast. - Smoother feed scrolling (Android): Enjoy a smoother experience when scrolling through your camera list—video feeds now pause and resume seamlessly as you move down the page. - Smoother camera history scrolling (iOS): Fixed a camera timeline issue on iOS where manually scrolling back to live video could occasionally get stuck on an empty historical frame - Accurate battery status indicators (iOS): Resolved an issue where live streaming cameras with unreadable battery levels would erroneously display a dead battery icon. - Performance improvements for Samsung phones: Fixed issue where camera audio stream used call volume instead of media volume. More on Google Home: - Google Home will fix broken Familiar Faces alerts on Walmart’s Onn cameras - Gemini for Home context memory expands to 15 mins, Nest Cam July 2026 update rolling out - Google Home app update makes automation easier, improves cameras, more Follow Ben: Twitter/X, Threads, Bluesky, and Instagram Comments

item.title: Google Play Store starts distributing third-party Android app stores – here’s how it works [Gallery]
item.description:
Source: 9to5Google Score: 5.40
Following a long battle in court, Google has opened the floodgates to third-party app store distribution via the Play Store in the US. Starting with just a single option, Aptoide Games, the Google Play Store will host and install third-party app and game stores on Android. This applies solely in the United States and third-party stores won’t show up everywhere – they’re only accessible via links or direct searches. Google explains on a support page: You can discover and download third-party app stores through a dedicated landing page in the Play Store. This is accessible via deep-links, your account menu in Google Play, the apps category page or via search queries (e.g., searching for “App Store” or for a specific store). Google adds that it “enforces its policies” from the Play Store on third-party stores, but that Google does not “review every app in these stores” nor manage updates or payments. As mentioned, the first store available is Aptoide Games, a mostly game-specific store full of free and paid titles. Installing the store works more or less like any other Android app, and, once installed, there are no additional security measures required for installing apps. We tested this by downloading “Clash of Kings” from Aptoide, and it works rather seamlessly. The only additional step is accepting the “Install” prompt when it shows up after the app is downloaded. So, while Epic Games was beat to the punch, it did get its wish. A way of getting third-party app stores a clean, frictionless way to install apps and games. More on Android: - Android’s upcoming ‘App Handles’ will bring clever multitasking to Pixel Fold [Video] - Google Assistant shutting down on Android and Wear OS in September - Google pushes for Android apps to better support ‘ultra-wide foldables’ like Galaxy Z Fold 8 Follow Ben: Twitter/X, Threads, Bluesky, and Instagram Comments

item.title: Google Wallet adds supervised balances for kids and teens, no bank account required
item.description:
Source: 9to5Google Score: 5.23
These days, the easiest way to pay for anything at practically any shop — save for Walmart, I suppose — is through the digital wallet stored on your phone or smartwatch. Of course, that makes it difficult for kids and teens to ever actually pay for anything on their own, especially if they don’t have their own bank account and your household is primarily cashless. With its latest update, that’s the exact problem Google Wallet is trying to fix. Starting today, parents in the US can rely on Google Wallet to set up a ‘secure balance’ for kids or teens under the age of 18, without requiring a fresh bank account. It’s essentially a digital allowance, with your child’s spending limits, account activity, and transactions all viewable from within your account. And while it doesn’t come with its own physical card — again, this isn’t a bank account — kids and teens can use their balance at any store that accepts Google Pay through tap to pay. In addition to the above safeguards, Google also supports optional notifications for purchases made by your child via Family Link, and allows for remote balance locks. That’s not just useful for whenever you need to put a stop to certain spending habits, but also ensures that a stolen or lost device (something that’s not particularly uncommon with younger users) doesn’t lead to losing out on cash as well. Google says it’s a “digital-first way” for kids to learn their earliest financial lessons without signing up for something like Greenlight or Acorns Early. This is just the latest way Google has tried to make managing finances easier for your children. Last year, Wallet began rolling out access for kids through Family Link, with access having first started on the kid-centric Fitbit Ace LTE. This change makes digital allowances that much easier, though the traditional experience should stick around as well. No word yet on if or when this will expand to parents outside the US. Comments

item.title: Google Messages rolling out long-press menu redesign with precise copying
item.description:
Source: 9to5Google Score: 5.04
After testing started in January, Google Messages is expanding beta access to a redesign of the long-press menu that aids one-handed usage. Previously, long-pressing a message would show a toolbar at the top of your screen. You’d see three actions at the right, with everything else in the three-dot overflow menu. Additionally, there’s the pill with emoji actions and Photomoji. Old The new design applies a blur effect to the background. Above the text or image, the emoji bar is unchanged. However, a menu now appears below with: - Reply - Forward - Copy - Star - Delete - Select more - Info - Save (for media) If there’s not enough space for the list, the selected item will appear higher up on the screen, complete with a bouncy animation. New Additionally, a second long-press on text will let you copy just a particular part of the message. You had to copy the entire message in the past. We’re seeing this menu redesign roll out with the latest version of the Google Messages beta (20260731_00_RC00) as part of a server-side update. If you’re not seeing it live yet, Force stop Google Messages from App info. More on Google Messages: - Google Messages will let you customize the shortcuts grid - Samsung Messages shuts down in favor of Google Messages on July 6 - iOS 27 will add inline replies & photo reactions to Android-iPhone RCS Comments

item.title: Google Contacts reveals what colors Pixel 11 HiLight will support
item.description:
Source: 9to5Google Score: 4.95
Ahead of the Pixel 11 launch, Google Contacts for Android has gained strings detailing upcoming support for HiLight. About APK Insight: In this “APK Insight” post, we’ve decompiled the latest version of an application that Google uploaded to the Play Store. When we decompile these files (called APKs, in the case of Android apps), we’re able to see various lines of code within that hint at possible future features. Keep in mind that Google may or may not ever ship these features, and our interpretation of what they are may be imperfect. We’ll try to enable those that are closer to being finished, however, to show you how they’ll look in case that they do ship. With that in mind, read on. Version 4.85 of Google Contacts outlines how the app will support HiLight, which is codenamed “glow” in strings, by letting you assign a “glow color” to your favorite contacts when they call. - <string name=”glow_enable_favorite_calls”>Tap to configure HiLight for favorite callers</string> - <string name=”glow_promo_card_subtitle”>Assign a custom glow color for when they call</string> - <string name=”glow_promo_card_title_no_contact_name”>Add a notification color</string> The available Pixel 11 HiLight colors are Blue, Cyan, Green, Orange, Pink, Purple, Teal, White, and Yellow. This lines up with recent leaks, where the other launch functionality is rumored to be Gemini status when the phone is face down. Support for HiLight in Google Contacts matches how Pixel VIPs is integrated with the app. Comments

item.title: Android Canary 2608 lets you customize Quick Settings layout on Pixel
item.description:

Google today is rolling out Android Canary 2608 with the ability to customize the Quick Settings layout. item.title: Android’s upcoming ‘App Handles’ will bring clever multitasking to Pixel Fold [Video]
item.description:
Source: 9to5Google Score: 4.85
Introduced in the latest Android Canary build, Google is preparing a new feature for foldables like the Pixel Fold series called “App Handles” which offers more flexible multitasking. Seemingly built on top of the functionality of Bubbles, “App Handles” are essentially a pinned app that’s attached to your taskbar, ready to be opened in the corner of your screen for easy access without messing with any of the content behind it. In an example shared on Twitter/X, the Calculator app on a Pixel Fold device is placed in an “App Handle” where it can be opened in a pop-up window along the right side of the screen while Chrome runs full-screen in the background. It can also be quickly shifted into a full-screen or split-screen format. It also looks like you can have more than one app in this format at onces, with a “+” button appearing next to the Calculator icon. This looks very useful, with this one example just scratching the surface. Having an app at the ready in a fixed location like this could be useful for note-taking apps, checking in on background tasks, and more. Existing features like Samsung’s pop-up windows and Google’s own Bubbles accomplish similar goals, but “App Handles” certainly offer a nice evolution to Android’s handling of multitasking. Right now, this is only live in the latest Android Canary build (2608), but it should arrive in future Android releases sometime down the road. item.title: Google Play adds Venmo as a payment method for apps, games, and more
item.description:
Source: 9to5Google Score: 4.78
Google has spent the past few years ramping up its efforts to get Android users to download more apps — and, in turn, to spend more cash on games, in-app purchases, and more. Today, Google is adding Venmo as an all-new way to make purchases on the Play Store, meaning that $40 you keep forgetting to transfer to your bank account just became your ticket to movie rentals, ad-free apps, and more. Google says Venmo users can link their account to the Play Store beginning today, allowing it to serve as an additional payment method for anything within the store. Alongside debit and credit cards, it joins Cash App and PayPal (which, as Venmo users have no doubt noticed through a cozier and cozier relationship, owns Venmo) as alternate payment methods available at checkout. Although Google doesn’t specify regions with this announcement, Venmo is effectively exclusive to the US, meaning this change really only affects US residents. Honestly, this move has taken a surprisingly long time to get here. Google added Cash App as a payment method on Play over two years ago now, and PayPal has been available as a billing option for over a decade. Still, for those of you who rely on Venmo for payments, cash transfers, and more, your digital wallet just opened up some new possibilities. item.description:

Google Photos rolled out the ability to convert photo subjects into stickers last year, indicated by a little “shimmer” animation. Now, Google is giving users the ability to turn off that animation. item.title: Zoom flaw let an attacker take over your device, including iPhone and Mac
item.description:
Source: 9to5Mac Score: 6.63
A Zoom vulnerability discovered with the help of an AI tool gave an attacker the ability to remotely execute code on whatever device a meeting participant was using, including both iPhone and Mac … Wired reports: Researchers [found] vulnerabilities in the video conferencing platform Zoom that could have been exploited to take over targets’ devices. Anyone on a call that involved screen sharing, whether participants or the host, would have been vulnerable to a silent attack that could be carried out with no indication and no interaction from the victim. [It] affected devices running all operating systems that Zoom supports—Windows, macOS, Linux, iOS, and Android. Cybersecurity firm A Security disclosed the vulnerability to Zoom and it has now been patched. However, it says the truly frightening thing was just how easy it was to use AI to find the flaw. The bug was discovered in early June using publicly available AI models, and it took fewer than 20 prompts to uncover the vulnerabilities and create a working attack […] A Security cofounder Omer Gull told WIRED ahead of the disclosure: “Before it would have taken a team of five people maybe six months with a lot of refining and iteration to find this. Now people can reach the same results with under 20 prompts. And Zoom is an important type of target because people assume trust when using it. They don’t see it as a threat.” Wired’s Lily Newman notes that Gull briefed her on the story in a video call taking place on … Microsoft Teams. Photo: LinkedIn/Unsplash Comments

item.title: Apple is working on a way to authenticate that a photo came from an iPhone camera
item.description:
Source: 9to5Mac Score: 6.53
References included in iOS 27 beta 5 point to a new feature designed to authenticate the camera source of an iPhone photo. Here are the details. Apple working on new Reference Image feature While the challenge posed by synthetic images trying to pass as authentic is not new, it has become an increasingly pressing issue with the rise of generative AI imagery. What used to take a skilled photo editor hours, or even days, can now be accomplished in seconds, with little more than a short prompt based on a half-formed idea. To address this, several companies have already introduced ways to make AI-generated content easier to identify. Google, for instance, developed SynthID, which embeds imperceptible watermarks into AI-generated images and other media. The technology has since expanded beyond Google’s own products, with companies including OpenAI adopting it for generated images. Likewise, Meta has introduced labels for AI-generated content across Facebook, Instagram, and Threads, though such systems have faced limitations in reliably identifying manipulated media, even when created by the company’s own AI models. Now, it appears that Apple might be gearing up to tackle the problem as well, in addition to “marking up” the metadata of images created via Image Playground. New code in iOS 27 beta 5 shows that the company is working on something called Apple Reference Image, which is designed to authenticate the source of photos using unique data tied to the iPhone camera hardware that captured them. In line with Apple’s privacy-focused approach to cloud-based processing of potentially sensitive user data, the company is designing Apple Reference Image in a way that prevents Apple from accessing the raw photo itself. Instead, the system sends the image to Private Cloud Compute for authentication, while only certain sensor information and photo metadata are sent back to Apple. Interestingly, if Apple determines that a sensor may have been compromised, it may revoke prior authentications associated with that sensor. As it stands, the feature is off by default, and once it’s live, it will be turned on via Settings > Camera > Reference Image, and tapping Reference Mode. Importantly, Reference mode must be used when capturing the photo via a new “Reference” mode in Camera. This means that photos taken normally won’t contain the provenance information needed to be authenticated later. Reference mode itself does not appear to authenticate the photo automatically. Instead, users can later choose to authenticate it, at which point the raw image and associated provenance data are sent to Private Cloud Compute for verification. During authentication, Apple assigns the photo a unique ID. Another privacy-focused aspect of the system is that authenticated photos can also be shared with others, whose Apple devices can check locally whether the photo remains authenticated, without telling Apple which images they are viewing. The information included when sharing may vary depending on the method used (AirDrop, Messages, etc.) and whether the photo is an original, edited, or authenticated version. Notably, if the user chooses to share “All Photos Data,” Apple says the transfer may also include unique hardware identifiers and any uncropped footage associated with the image. Apple is also adding a “Transfer with Provenance” option for USB transfers. When enabled, authenticated photos transferred to a Mac or PC will include their Reference Image data, while unauthenticated photos may still carry provenance information such as unique hardware identifiers and any uncropped footage. What’s your take on Apple Reference Image? Let us know in the comments. Comments

item.title: Report: Non-gaming apps drove mobile spending growth in Q2 as games fell 4.5%
item.description:
Source: 9to5Mac Score: 5.67
A new report from Sensor Tower shows that non-gaming apps continued to drive global mobile spending growth in Q2 2026 across iOS and Android, while gaming revenue declined 4.5% year over year. Here are the details. AI apps lead non-gaming growth as mobile game spending declines Last month, during Apple’s fiscal Q3 2026 earnings call, the company attributed part of its Services revenue slowdown to weaker mobile gaming performance and regulatory changes affecting the App Store business model. Today, Sensor Tower published its Q2 2026 Digital Market Index report, offering a closer look at how mobile app spending and downloads changed during the quarter. According to the report, non-gaming revenue rose 14.6% year over year in Q2 2026, while gaming revenue declined 4.5% over the same period. In absolute terms, non-gaming apps generated $24.4 billion in revenue and 25.5 billion downloads, compared with $19.2 billion in revenue and 11.3 billion downloads for games. The report also noted that U.S. IAP revenue declined 3% year over year, but the country still led the world in spending at $14.8 billion. China came in a distant second at $5.98 billion, despite seeing revenue grow 10% over the same period. When it came to the top markets by app downloads, India remained in first place with 6.67 billion installs, up 4% year over year. The U.S. followed with 3.08 billion downloads, down 0.2%, while Brazil ranked third with 2.43 billion, down 2%. As for which app categories generated the most revenue, here’s what Sensor Tower said: Non-gaming genres maintained strong monetization momentum in Q2 2026, with nine of the top 10 categories posting positive YoY growth. Generative AI led this expansion, doubling consumer spend with a 108% YoY surge. Market leader ChatGPT held roughly 60% category revenue share with 82% YoY growth, while competitors like Claude, Grok, and Gemini also saw rapid acceleration. Claude particularly stood out, climbing from No. 7 ranked Generative AI app in Q2 2025 to No. 2 globally in Q2 2026. Dating & Social Discovery was the only top category to experience a decline globally, falling 11% YoY primarily due to softness in the US market, which contracted 34% YoY. However, Latin American markets showed strong growth momentum, led by Mexico with a 41% YoY revenue gain, alongside double-digit expansion in Brazil (+19% YoY) and Argentina (+18% YoY). Sensor Tower says the world’s most downloaded app for the period was ChatGPT, followed by TikTok and Instagram, while the top IAP revenue apps were TikTok, ChatGPT, and Google One. Claude took the top spot among breakout apps by IAP revenue growth, jumping 34 places to No. 10 overall, while PineDrama saw the biggest breakout in downloads, climbing 237 places to No. 20 worldwide. For Sensor Tower’s full Q2 2026 Digital Market Index report, follow this link. Comments

item.title: Apple faces class action lawsuit for ‘fraud’ over iCloud Private Relay flaw
item.description:
Source: 9to5Mac Score: 5.41
Security researchers last week revealed a flaw in Apple’s iCloud Private Relay feature. While this is supposed to protect your IP address from the websites you visit, a vulnerability means that it often fails to do so. Any time there’s a problem with an Apple product or service, a class action lawsuit is sure to follow, and this is no exception … What is iCloud Private Relay? As we’ve explained previously, iCloud Private Relay isn’t quite a VPN, but it is intended to fulfil a similar privacy function in terms of preventing your web usage being tracked when you are using Safari as your browser. Here’s how Apple describes it: - Your IP address is visible to your network provider and to the first relay, which is operated by Apple. Your DNS records are encrypted, so neither party can see the address of the website you’re trying to visit. - The second relay, which is operated by a third-party content provider, generates a temporary IP address, decrypts the name of the website you requested, and connects you to the site. In other words, your ISP sees only that you are accessing an Apple server, and the website you visit sees only an IP address generated by that server. What’s the flaw? Security researchers found that any website that supports passkeys can see your real IP address. In a quirk of how passkeys work, a user’s device makes a web request outside of the browser itself. Meaning, that request essentially bypasses Private Relay and exposes a user’s real IP address, even though to them it may look like they are simply interacting with a website as normal. Worse, it doesn’t even matter whether the website actually supports passkeys: just pretending it does so will reveal your IP address. The class action lawsuit A class action lawsuit accusing Apple of false advertising, misrepresentation, and fraud has now been filed by Clarkson Law Firm – the same lawyers who previously obtained a $250M settlement over the delayed launch of Siri AI. [Apple] knew, or should have known, that the Challenged Representations were false, misleading, deceptive, and unlawful, at the time that Defendant manufactured, marketed, advertised, labeled, and sold the [iCloud+] Subscriptions. Tim Giordano, a partner at Clarkson, told us the firm considers it an “outrageous betrayal of consumer trust.” “Apple built its entire brand on the promise that it would protect its users’ privacy when no other company would. For Apple’s iCloud users to now learn that for years they were paying Apple a premium for a protection that simply didn’t work, exposing them to the very tracking, profiling, and targeting Apple warned them about, is an outrageous violation and betrayal of consumer trust and law.” We’ve reached out to Apple for comment and will update with any response. Comments

item.title: iOS 27 public beta 3 is here with Siri AI, iPhone speed upgrades, and more
item.description:
Source: 9to5Mac Score: 5.30
The third iOS 27 public beta is now available for iPhone. It gives users an early chance to try Apple’s biggest software update of the year. Siri AI is the headline feature. The release also includes a redesigned Screen Time experience, Liquid Glass refinements, performance upgrades, and dozens of quality-of-life changes. Here’s how to install the beta, what’s new, and which features you should try first. How to join the iOS 27 public beta The Apple Beta Software Program is free, and you don’t need a developer account. Before you begin, back up your iPhone to iCloud or a computer. Beta software can include bugs, reduced battery life, and third-party app compatibility problems. To join and install the beta: - Visit the Apple Beta Software Program website and choose Sign Up or Sign In. - Sign in with the same Apple Account you use on your iPhone. Then accept the program terms and enroll your account. - Open Settings on your iPhone. - Go to General > Software Update > Beta Updates. - Select iOS 27 Public Beta. - Return to the Software Update screen, then tap Update Now when the beta appears. Apple recommends installing beta software on a secondary device. If you use your primary iPhone, make sure you have a recent backup first. iOS 27 supports every iPhone that runs iOS 26. That includes iPhone 11 and newer, plus iPhone SE (2nd generation and later). However, Apple Intelligence requires iPhone 15 Pro or newer. Apple’s most powerful new on-device model has an even shorter compatibility list, but Siri AI only requires Apple Intelligence compatibility to work. Siri AI is the biggest iOS 27 feature Once the iOS 27 public beta is installed, Siri AI is the best place to start. Apple has rebuilt Siri around its next-generation Apple Intelligence system. The assistant can now hold an ongoing conversation and search your personal information. It can also understand onscreen content, take actions in apps, and answer broader questions. Siri responses emerge from the Dynamic Island. Pull down on a response to open the full conversation. Meanwhile, a standalone Siri app keeps your history in one place. It syncs that history privately through iCloud. After installing the public beta, ask Siri to find a detail buried in Mail, Messages, Notes, Reminders, or Calendar. Then ask a follow-up without repeating the original context. In iOS 27 beta 3, Siri also gained early access to information from some third-party apps. The Camera app adds a Siri mode for Visual Intelligence. For example, you can photograph a membership barcode and turn it into a Wallet pass. Siri can also import events from a flyer. In addition, Apple has added controls for Siri’s pace and expressivity. You’ll find them under Settings > Siri > Voice. These settings also affect spoken output in Maps and Safari. Siri AI initially supports select English variants, and it won’t launch in the EU right away. It also requires an Apple Intelligence-compatible iPhone. Some advanced on-device features require iPhone 17 Pro, iPhone 17 Pro Max, or iPhone Air. Apple Intelligence upgrades more iPhone apps The iOS 27 public beta spreads some of its best AI features beyond Siri. Safari can automatically organize tabs by topic. It also groups bookmarks and Reading List items while surfacing recently closed topics on the Start Page. In addition, Notify Me can watch a webpage for a change, such as an item coming back in stock. Safari can even create a specialized extension from a natural-language description. Photos adds three powerful editing tools. Clean Up handles larger and more complex distractions. Extend generates content beyond the existing frame. Finally, Spatial Reframing lets you adjust the apparent camera position after taking a picture. Try Extend on a photo with a crooked horizon. After that, test Spatial Reframing on a portrait with an awkward composition. The Passwords app can automatically replace eligible weak or compromised passwords. It handles verification codes and shows its progress in a Live Activity. Shortcuts can now build an automation from a plain-language request. You can continue describing changes to refine the result. Other Apple Intelligence additions include: - Call Context in Phone, which surfaces details such as reservation numbers when you call a business. - Photorealistic generation and natural-language editing in Image Playground. - Natural-language event creation and editing in Calendar. iOS 27 makes Liquid Glass more customizable iOS 27 doesn’t replace the Liquid Glass design introduced last year. Instead, Apple has focused on clarity and flexibility. Controls now diffuse complicated background content more effectively. Darker edges and brighter highlights also create better separation. As a result, buttons and text should remain easier to read. App icons have more layers and definition, too. The feature to try first is the new Liquid Glass customization slider. You’ll find it under Settings > Appearance. It ranges from ultra-clear to fully tinted and applies across iOS and third-party apps. iOS 27 should feel faster, even on older iPhones Apple’s promised iOS 27 speed improvements extend beyond its newest hardware. The company says apps can launch up to 30% faster. Nearby AirDrop transfers can finish up to 80% faster. New captures can also appear in Photos up to 70% faster. Apple optimized the CPU scheduler all the way back to iPhone 11. In addition, unlocking, Home Screen navigation, Control Center scrolling, and Lock Screen switching should feel smoother. Camera launches faster in Low Power Mode as well. iOS 27 also moves between Wi-Fi and cellular data more intelligently. Therefore, your iPhone should be less likely to cling to a weak network as you leave home. Apple rebuilt search across Spotlight, Photos, and Mail, too. Mail now displays up to five ranked Top Results. Screen Time and child safety get a major overhaul iOS 27 is bringing a major Screen Time and parental-control overhaul. The new dashboard will give parents a clearer look at a child’s activity. It will also offer one-tap access changes. Time Allowances will set limits for categories such as Games, Entertainment, and Social Media. Meanwhile, Schedules will control which apps are available at different times. Parents will be able to create separate routines for school days, evenings, and weekends. Ask to Browse will extend the familiar Ask to Buy flow to websites. Children can also request permission before contacting someone new. Communication Safety already detects and blurs nudity. In iOS 27, it also intervenes when it detects gore or violent content. One caveat is important. The redesigned experience requires the participating Family Sharing devices to run the OS 27 generation. More iOS 27 public beta features to try The smaller improvements add up quickly: - Messages continues sending large media in the background without blocking newer texts. It also consolidates group-chat Tapback notifications. - Photos adds full-resolution Shared Albums, Windows and Android contributions, keywords, star ratings, and customizable slideshows. - You can save any video frame as a photo with one tap. - Alarm volume can be adjusted independently of system volume. - Extra-large widgets can fill an entire Home Screen page. - AirPods gain a custom equalizer for lows, mids, and highs. - iPhone can connect directly to compatible GymKit equipment. - FaceTime supports simultaneous front- and rear-camera video on iPhone Air and iPhone 17 models. - Home adds more reliable HomeKit Secure Video recording and native 4K camera support with eligible hardware and iCloud+ service. The iOS 27 public beta will continue changing throughout the summer. Apple plans to release the final version this fall. If you find a problem, use the built-in Feedback Assistant app to report it directly to Apple. What to expect in iOS 27 public beta 3 You can see what’s new in iOS 27 beta 5, which should be the same as today’s iOS 27 public beta 3 release. Do more with your Apple products Comments

While WhatsApp has long offered a search option in the chat info screen, the app is now working on a faster way to access it directly from a conversation. Here are the details. WhatsApp works on a faster search flow on iOS As WhatsApp users probably know, there are two main ways to search for past messages in the app. The first is from the main chats list, where a search query looks across all conversations. Now, as spotted by WABetaInfo, the app may soon add a faster way to find past messages within a conversation. item.title: Making sense of the conflicting 20th anniversary iPhone reports
item.description:
Source: 9to5Mac Score: 5.11
Yesterday saw two conflicting reports about next year’s 20th anniversary iPhone, said to embody Apple’s long-term vision of “a single slab of glass.” There have already been contradictory reports about exactly what we should expect, but yesterday’s disagreement was the biggest yet … The story so far Former Apple design chief Jony Ive frequently referred to his long-term vision of the iPhone effectively becoming a single slab of glass. The company is widely believed to have retained this vision beyond Ive’s departure. While Apple generally isn’t noted for making a big deal of its various product birthdays, the consensus view is that it’s aiming to get as close as possible to this vision in time for the iPhone’s 20th anniversary. This is likely to include embedding the Face ID tech beneath the display, with the possibility of the front-facing camera likewise being hidden beneath the screen. We’ve already seen conflicting reports about what to expect, however. While it was initially thought that this would be a standalone model along the lines of the iPhone Air and upcoming iPhone Ultra, more recent reporting has suggested that this design will instead be used for next year’s iPhone Pro models. Sequentially, this would be the iPhone 19 Pro, but it’s possible Apple may want to mark the anniversary by skipping this and jumping straight to the iPhone 20 naming. Yesterday’s conflicting reports Things got a little more confusing yesterday when an analyst suggested that Apple had given up on the idea of launching an all-glass iPhone next year. While Jefferies once viewed the release of an all-glass iPhone as plausible, Lee believes development has come to a halt. According to the analyst, supply chain checks suggest the project was cancelled due to low yield. However, Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman was quick to contradict this. Apple Inc. is still planning to offer a glass-centric overhaul of the iPhone for the device’s 20th anniversary, people familiar with the matter said, countering an analyst report that the move had been canceled […] Though Apple’s vision for an iPhone with uninterrupted glass has proven challenging to execute, [its] product road map hasn’t changed. The likely reality The key point here is that there is not a single final destination for Apple’s vision of the iPhone. Whatever the company plans for next year, it will only ever be one or more steps closer to that sci-fi vision of “a single slab of glass.” The question is not whether that box will be ticked next year, but instead how much progress we see the company make toward its vision. But whether it is one step closer or several, it certainly won’t be the last one in the evolution of the iPhone design. Indeed, Gurman indicated that Apple has taken a step back from the point it had originally hoped to reach by next year. A more aspirational version championed by Apple’s design studio used even more glass, instead of metal, but was scrapped early on. With that approach, the company encountered problems connecting the glass panels together. The design didn’t hold up when Apple had to figure out how to produce it at large volumes, according to the people. It’s very likely that the Jefferies analyst heard the same thing, but only relatively recently, and took this to mean complete abandonment of the plan. My own expectation is that next year’s design will be a major step forward – the equivalent of the launch of the iPhone X – but that there will be much more to come in subsequent years. The big question to me is whether the 2027 iPhone will be a sufficient leap for Apple to apply some special branding, be that labelling it as a 20th anniversary iPhone (very unlikely, in my view), giving it some other special name, or skipping a generation to call it the iPhone 20. What’s your expectation? Please share your thoughts in the comments. Comments

item.title: Grok Bot is an all-new iPhone and Mac app from SpaceXAI and Cursor
item.description:
Source: 9to5Mac Score: 5.01
SpaceXAI and Cursor are in the process of becoming a single company, but first, the two firms are releasing an all-new iPhone and Mac app called Grok Bot. According to SpaceXAI’s announcement, Grok Bot is a new kind of AI agent described as “AI teammates you can give real work to.” Each Bot gets its own computer, then signs into the apps and services you already use to take on work across inboxes and other tools. SpaceXAI says Bots can complete jobs end to end, only returning when approval is needed. You can message one “like a colleague,” the company says, and the agent will remember conversations, learn preferences, and improve with more use. Grok Bot launches in beta today on Mac and iOS. Windows and Linux desktop versions are also available. Android is listed as coming soon. Access is initially restricted to SuperGrok Heavy, Cursor Ultra, and Cursor Teams Premium subscribers. You can learn more from the official announcement here. Do more with your Apple products Comments

item.title: The new iOS 27 beta further expands Siri voice customization options
item.description:
Source: 9to5Mac Score: 4.93
iOS 27 beta 5 has further expanded the new Siri voice customization options. In earlier betas, the new Pace and Expressivity sliders were only available for the two newly-introduced Siri voices that have an American accent. But now, the customization is available for any American voice, and all of the existing British accent voices as well … That means there are now eleven supported voices which allow for choosing different pace (speed of talking) and expressivity (the amount of emotion and emphasis) settings. You can customize Pace and Expressivity by going to Settings -> Siri -> Voice and dragging the sliders. There are five supported levels for both pace and expressivity. On a modern iPhone, that means there are a total of eight American voice options and four British voices to pick from, that support pace and expressivity adjustments. Apple previously indicated that the new Siri voices take advantage of a new powerful on-device model, but it has pretty recent hardware requirements. The feature requires an iPhone 17 Pro, iPhone 17 Air, iPad Pro (M4) and newer, and Macs with M3 chip or newer and at least 12 GB RAM. Siri AI itself requires an iPhone 15 Pro or newer; you just get the older voice synthesis on older hardware. Siri AI will be launching in beta sometime later this year. Comments

item.title: iOS 27 code reveals six unreleased iPhone models coming soon
item.description:
Source: 9to5Mac Score: 4.88
Apple released iOS 27 beta 5 yesterday, with changes including new app icons and Spotlight design tweaks. As it turns out, the update also includes references to all the new iPhone models expected to be released over the next six to eight months. Unreleased iPhone references As first spotted by Macworld, iOS 27 beta 5 references six unreleased iPhones spanning the entire iPhone 18 lineup, the iPhone Air 2, and the forthcoming foldable iPhone Ultra. The references were found in “system files related to the iPhone’s battery drivers and Battery Intelligence features.” The code references include only Apple’s internal identifiers (V62, V63, etc), not the marketing names. Based on other leaks, however, you can correlate those model identifiers to their expected marketing names: - V62: iPhone Air 2 - V63: iPhone 18 Pro - V64: iPhone 18 Pro Max - V67: iPhone 18 - V68: iPhone Ultra (or iPhone Fold) - V69: iPhone 18e The update doesn’t include any further information about these devices. Apple is expected to kick off the iPhone 18 cycle next month with the launch of the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max. The iPhone Ultra is also expected to be announced next month. The iPhone 18, iPhone 18e, and iPhone Air 2 are reportedly slated for sometime in early 2027. This marks the first year of Apple’s rearranged iPhone release schedule, splitting the launches into two windows over the course of the full year. What new iPhone model are you most excited for Apple to launch? Are you intrigued by the iPhone Ultra? Let us know down in the comments. Chance’s favorites: Follow Chance: Threads, Bluesky, Instagram, and Mastodon. Comments

item.title: Court rejects Apple’s attempt to postpone App Store fee proceedings in Epic Games case [U]
item.description:
Source: 9to5Mac Score: 4.80
Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney says Judge Yvonne Gonzalez Rogers has rejected Apple’s request to pause the App Store fee proceedings pending the Supreme Court’s review of the company’s contempt ruling. Here are the details. Apple now has 24 hours to file proposed App Store fee Last month, Apple filed a motion to pause the proceedings that will determine what commission, if any, it can charge on purchases completed outside the App Store. This is part of the ongoing lawsuit between Epic Games and Apple, in which Apple was found in contempt for imposing a 27% commission on purchases made through external links after Judge Yvonne Gonzalez Rogers ordered the company to allow developers to direct users to alternative payment methods. Apple appealed the contempt finding to the Supreme Court. After the Court agreed to hear the case, Apple asked Judge Gonzalez Rogers to pause the lower-court proceedings, arguing that the eventual Supreme Court ruling could affect any work done in the meantime. In its response to Apple’s request, Epic argued that the court should deny the motion for stay, saying the proceedings should move forward regardless of the Supreme Court’s review. The filing also noted that Apple had already agreed to submit its proposed fee and supporting evidence within 24 hours if the stay request was denied. Apple, for its part, further attempted to persuade the court by citing a recent decision in another Northern District of California case that was stayed because the judge agreed that it could be affected by the same Supreme Court review. Now, as Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney noted in a post on X, Judge Gonzalez Rogers denied Apple’s request. In practice, this means Apple now has 24 hours to file its proposed fee, the calculations behind it, and evidence explaining why the court should approve it. Apple has yet to comment on the decision, and Judge Gonzalez Rogers’s ruling has also yet to be made public. We reached out to Apple for comment and will update this post if we hear back or once the order becomes publicly available. Update, 8:15 p.m. ET: Judge Gonzalez Rogers’s ruling is now publicly available. In her decision, she says that “the Supreme Court’s grant of a narrow review of the contempt proceedings does not substantially impact the factual issues that must be resolved to ensure compliance with the injunction,” adding that the fact that “Apple agreed to file its evidentiary proffer within 24 hours of this Court’s decision reveals Apple is prepared to proceed.” She also takes a swipe at Apple’s approach to the proceedings, citing it as part of a broader pattern of delay in the case: Given Apple’s propensity to delay, this phase will likely take time. We are approaching the five-year anniversary of this Court’s decision. Further delay is unwarranted. You can read Judge Gonzalez Rogers’s ruling in full below: Comments

item.title: Sonos is planning Ace Ultra headphones with a big AI push, report says
item.description:
Source: 9to5Mac Score: 4.80
Two years ago, Sonos made the leap from wireless speakers to over-ear headphones. Now it sounds like Sonos is preparing a more premium, AI-infused encore. Sonos Ace Ultra headphones are on the way Chris Welch reports for Bloomberg that Sonos is developing the Sonos Ace Ultra, a higher-end follow-up to its 2024 Ace headphones. An FCC filing spotted Monday names the product and points to as many as five color options, up from the black and white finishes offered on the original model. Sonos has a September product launch planned, and the timing of the filing suggests the Ace Ultra could be part of that event. The filing also contains technical clues that the new headphones may support voice commands. Bloomberg reports that CEO Tom Conrad has acknowledged that the original headphones arrived without enough whole-home integration or differentiation in a crowded category. This time, Sonos appears to be tying the hardware more directly to its broader AI ambitions. Conrad has described the company’s opportunity as conversational computing and predictive intelligence in the home, with Sonos devices serving as hardware that can work across rooms and understand how a household lives. The company has already expanded Sonos Voice Control with Philips Hue and Lutron Caseta controls. Meanwhile, Apple’s upgraded AirPods Max 2 arrived in March with the H2 chip, stronger noise cancellation, and Live Translation. Siri AI will extend to AirPods as part of iOS 27 as well. For more on the upcoming Sonos Ace Ultra headphones, check out the Bloomberg report in full here. Do more with your Apple products Comments

item.title: macOS 27 Golden Gate beta 5 now available to developers
item.description:
Source: 9to5Mac Score: 4.78
Continuing Apple’s beta rollouts ahead of the official launch of macOS 27 Golden Gate later this year, Apple has now released the fifth beta of the OS to developers. Here’s what to expect. Apple rolls out macOS 27 beta 5 Three weeks ago, Apple released macOS 27 Golden Gate beta 4 and, just a couple of days later, its corresponding public beta. Now, the company is rolling out macOS Golden Gate beta 5, continuing its push to fix bugs and performance issues as it prepares for the official release later this year. macOS 27 Golden Gate introduces the new Siri app, alongside the revamped Siri AI. It also features the new AI-powered Shortcuts app, which accepts natural-language prompts to create shortcuts, as well as a prompt-based Safari extension builder. Additionally, macOS 27 Golden Gate introduces new Golden Gate-themed wallpapers and screensavers, while reverting to fixed-radius corners for windows and apps. That reverses a change made in macOS 26, which adjusted corner radii based on the contents of each window’s or app’s menu bar. The build version for macOS 27 Golden Gate beta 5 is 26A5406e. We are digging through the new beta and will report back with what we find. Installing the macOS 27 Golden Gate beta Here’s how to install the macOS 27 Golden Gate developer beta 5: - Back up your Mac - Open System Settings - Go to General ⇾ Software Update - Click the ‘i’ icon next to Beta Updates - From the dropdown menu in the top-right, select the macOS Developer Golden Gate Beta - Hit ‘Done’ Did you spot anything new in today’s macOS 27 Golden Gate beta? Let us know in the comments. Comments

item.title: Apple considers round screens and more radical designs for future Apple Watch revamp
item.description:
Source: 9to5Mac Score: 4.68
Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman goes into some detail today about the future for the Apple Watch product line. He suggests Apple is going back to the drawing board as the Watch faces stiffer competition from the likes of the Oura Ring and other screenless smart fitness devices. It seems Apple is preparing to revamp the concept of the Apple Watch from the ground up … Although it sounds like plans haven’t been finalized, Apple is considering all sorts of shapes and sizes, including watches with circular round displays, fitness accessories that have no screens at all, and more. This would represent a major breakpoint in the history of the Apple Watch, as every model up to now has basically revolved around the same basic design concept. Bloomberg indicates Apple is looking at possibilities on the low-end and the high-end, weighing up the appeal of both more premium and more affordable models. The new wearable form factors would also intersect with a software revamp, in which Apple is looking to push the Health app in a more AI-centric direction. Top comment by AnthonyG Sure, make a health bracelet for people who don't wear a Watch. Round watches have issues. Looking at 'smartwatch' information on a round screen is lousy. One reason I don't like competitor products is because they’re round. Round is for traditional watches. However, nothing is close to shipping. It doesn’t even sound like Apple has decided on something concretely as of yet. So anything radically new is still years away from coming to market. This fall, Apple will release new iterative models of the Watch, including Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4. These will feature new CPUs, some new color options and improved fitness features. The new Watches will probably launch at the company’s annual September event, which will also be the venue for the unveiling of the new iPhone 18 Pro and the first foldable iPhone, potentially branded as ‘iPhone Ultra’. Comments

item.title: Apple rolls out macOS 27 Golden Gate public beta 3, here’s how to install it
item.description:
Source: 9to5Mac Score: 4.66
Users enrolled in Apple’s public beta program can now install macOS 27 Golden Gate public beta 3. Here’s what’s new in the system. macOS 27 Golden Gate public beta 3 now available After yesterday’s release of macOS 27 Golden Gate beta 5 for developers, Apple is now rolling out that same version as the system’s third public beta. Yesterday’s beta didn’t include any major new features, but it did revamp several icons, including Siri, Activity Monitor, Safari, the App Store, and Chess. macOS 27 Golden Gate introduces the new Siri app, alongside the revamped Siri AI assistant. It also features prompt-based Shortcuts and Safari extensions creation, and allows users to control the Liquid Glass intensity with a slider during setup, or in System Settings. The update also standardizes corner radii across windows and apps, addressing a common complaint about macOS Tahoe 26. Apps and windows now use the same fixed radius, rather than adjusting it based on the items in the title bar. The release build for macOS 27 Golden Gate public beta 3 is 26A5406e, which is the same as the current developer build. Installing macOS 27 Golden Gate’s public beta Here’s how to install the macOS 27 Golden Gate public beta 3: - Enroll your Mac on the public beta program on https://beta.apple.com - Go to System Settings ⇾ General Software ⇾ Update - Click the ‘i’ button next to Beta Updates - From the dropdown menu in the top-right, select the macOS 27 Golden Gate Public Beta - Hit ‘Done’ Did you spot any changes in the new beta? Let us know in the comments. Comments

item.title: NWS-San Diego says, 'When Thunder Roars, Go Indoors,' with possibly thunderstorms
item.description:
Source: ABC 10News San Diego Score: 5.50
JULIAN, Calif. (KGTV) – Julian can bring visitors from all over Southern California and beyond the Golden State. “We just wanted to enjoy some, you know, apple pie and some good food. We also wanted a little bit of a small-town feel,” Jillian LeDuff, who was visiting from Long Beach, said. It was a hot and humid Monday in the mountain town. But, the weather is also expected to be brewing other conditions for Julian and the rest of the mountain region. “This afternoon and again tomorrow afternoon, we are expecting some widespread monsoonal thunderstorms over the mountains,” Sam Zuber, a meteorologist with National Weather Service - San Diego, said. Zuber said these two days of expected rain on Monday and Tuesday could bring some flooding potential and thunderstorms. “There's limited road networks, and so if you don't have to go out during the afternoon hours, I would avoid if you could,” Zuber said.“When we're dealing with fires in the fire season as well, another thing that we worry about are burn scars. And so any areas that have recently burned or seen massive fires, any rainfall that kind of goes over them could result in some localized debris flows as well.” Jillian LeDuff and Corey Huber told ABC 10News that they and their dog Honey have already felt the showers during their stay in Julian. “It kind of hit us out of nowhere, so we had to actually walk back to the car, grab the umbrella,” Huber said. “Yeah, we got what we needed yesterday, and so we're trying to get everything done before we head out now.” If you are out and about in the mountains or close to home, the National Weather Service said if you hear thunder, get inside as soon as you do. “Lightning can strike pretty far away from any thunderstorm, so we recommend that if you hear thunder, you are close enough to be struck by lightning,” Zuber said. “Now, we recommend that you also stay inside for at least 30 minutes after the last, uh, crackle of thunder that you hear. And then that's the way to make sure that you stay safe from any kind of lightning threat.” Obviously, another tried-and-true phrase with the possibility for these storms is, “Turn Around, Don’t Drown.” You never know just how deep the water on the roadway is or how much it has been eroded away by those flood waters.

item.title: The Streamline: San Diego Unified students head back to school
item.description:
Source: ABC 10News San Diego Score: 5.34
Here is what you need to know in the August 10, 2026, Streamline newsletter: - It’s Back to School time for the San Diego Unified School District, and with the first day of classes comes some major changes students will have to get used to. - Iran is insisting that the U.S. meet its demands in negotiations before the Strait of Hormuz reopens. - Two years after a fire destroyed her home and took her son’s life, a San Marcos mother is finally returning home and sharing the emotional journey of rebuilding her life. WEEKEND WRAP-UP TOP STORY Nearly 100,000 San Diego Unified students will return to classes Monday, with some major changes awaiting children going back to school, including revised technology policies. Following the district's Phone-free School Day policy last year, the district's "Learner-Centered Technology initiative" is intended to change how district-issued devices are used in schools. District-issued Chromebooks will now have video-streaming platforms such as YouTube blocked unless enabled by teachers for specific instructional activities. Non-instructional gaming platforms will also be blocked and computer carts will be removed from transitional kindergarten classrooms. Students with Individualized Education Programs, Section 504 Plans, or language-learning needs will continue to receive "appropriate access" to technology, a district statement read. "Back-to-school is an opportunity to establish healthy routines that help students succeed throughout the year," said Richard Barrera, president of the San Diego Unified Board of Education. "Technology has transformed education in many positive ways, but it works best when it is used with purpose. These changes help ensure our classrooms remain places where students are actively engaged with their teachers, collaborating with classmates, and building the skills they need for success in school and beyond." District-issued devices will use Blocksi, a digital safety platform that filters inappropriate content. "Learning doesn't begin by interacting with a screen. It begins with curiosity, meaningful relationships, and engaging face-to-face instruction," said Shana Hazan, trustee of SDUSD's school board. "These changes are designed to ensure technology serves as a tool that supports learning while giving students more opportunities to think critically, collaborate with one another, and build the communication skills they'll use for the rest of their lives." The existing phone policy prohibits the use of phones during school hours depending on each school's bell schedule. Phone use is permitted before and after school on campus, and high schools will allow use of phones before the first bell, during lunch and passing periods. Additionally, district leaders said SDUSD will focus on four priorities: student wellness, literacy, mathematics and college and career readiness. "Every new school year is an opportunity to reimagine what is possible for our students," said Superintendent Fabi Bagula. "This year, we are making meaningful investments in the whole child -- strengthening student wellness, expanding literacy and mathematics achievement, and creating even more opportunities for students to discover their passions and prepare for college, careers, and life. When students feel healthy, supported, challenged, and connected, there is no limit to what they can accomplish." New efforts will include information campaigns to focus on the importance of sleep, hydration and physical activity to learning, a preschool curriculum designed to nurture early language and literacy development through play and exploration and relaunching the 6th grade middle school math curriculum with a focused approach on integrating online, paper, and hands-on experiences, the district statement read. "Student wellness is not separate from academic achievement, it makes academic achievement possible," said Susan Barndollar, the district's executive director of nursing and wellness. "Every investment we make in supporting students' physical health, mental health, nutrition, relationships, and sense of belonging helps create classrooms where students are ready to learn and able to reach their full potential." After years of declining enrollment, SDUSD more than doubled its new enrollment goal for the 2026-27 school year. During the month of July, 1,950 new students enrolled in San Diego Unified schools, adding to the 1,083 students who enrolled during June. The district's goal was to enroll 1,309 new students -- the number of students who have left the district since the 2024-25 school year. "Every new student who joins San Diego Unified brings new dreams, talents, and possibilities to our schools, and we couldn't be more excited to welcome more than 3,000 new students and their families to our community this year," Bagula said. "Choosing a school is one of the most important decisions a family makes, and we are honored they chose San Diego Unified. From enrollment on, we want every family to feel they belong here. Our educators and staff are ready to welcome each student, provide exceptional learning opportunities, and support them as they learn, grow, and thrive." According to the California Department of Education, public school enrollment declined by nearly 75,000 students statewide, while the Education Commission of the States reports national public school enrollment has fallen by 1.18 million students over the past five years. Enrollment remains open throughout the school year. Families interested in enrolling can visit SanDiegoUnified.org/Enroll or call 619-260- 2410 for assistance. San Diego Unified serves 175 schools from preschool through grade 12. Story by City News Service MICROCLIMATE FORECASTS Coasts Inland Mountains Deserts BREAKING OVERNIGHT (AP) — An Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesperson said Iran will not reopen the Strait of Hormuz until the United States met its conditions. “It is up to the U.S. side to stop and make amends for its illegal and destructive actions,” Esmail Baghaei said Monday, noting the American blockade of Iranian ports. Iran wants the U.S. to lift the blockade, pay compensation for months of war damage, lift economic sanctions and release Iran's frozen assets. The closure of the Strait of Hormuz — a waterway that normally carries roughly one-fifth of the world's traded oil supplies — has become the war’s most lasting consequence. The impasse has kept energy prices as a major focus of U.S. politics ahead of November’s midterm elections. Iran is holding separate talks with Oman over transit through the strait, including potentially a temporary shipping corridor. But it has said any actual reopening is contingent on talks with the U.S. Israel declares closed military zone in Taybeh Israel's military said Monday it had declared a Christian-majority town in the occupied West Bank a closed military zone to keep out Israeli settlers and other non-residents. The new tactic is designed to keep Israelis out of Taybeh, which is surrounded by settlements to its east and west and has been subject to arson, vandalism and settlers coming onto private and village property. The order does not apply to Palestinian residents or journalists, who the army said would be allowed unless soldiers determine their presence poses a threat. The army said its troops would detain suspects and disperse gatherings to keep the peace. The designation comes after months of the army and police struggling to maintain order throughout the territory, where at least 87 Palestinians have been killed by Israeli settlers or soldiers in 2026, according to the Ramallah-based Palestinian Health Ministry. Parts of Taybeh lie in what's called “Area B” where Israel maintains security control, but residents have complained that the army and police are slow to respond to attacks by extremist settlers. Yemen provides death toll on Sunday's Houthi attack on Red Sea town Yemen's Iran-backed Houthi rebels attacked a Red Sea port town controlled by government forces on Sunday, killing seven and injuring 30 people. Yemen’s Defense Ministry — which operates under its internationally recognized government — said four military personnel and three civilians were killed. The attack on Mokha is the latest in one of the largest waves of Houthi strikes on Yemeni military positions and areas held by the Saudi-backed government since a 2022 truce. It comes as threats to shipping through the Strait of Hormuz have renewed focus on the Red Sea and Bab el-Mandeb Strait at its southern tip. Some shipping has shifted toward that route with Hormuz largely off limits to traffic. Beekeepers try to restart honey production in Gaza More than two years of war in Gaza flattened most of the territory and destroyed sectors of the economy, but beekeepers are now beginning to rebuild their businesses. Before the start of the Israel-Hamas war, the sector was based in agricultural lands near the perimeter of the strip, which today remains under the control of Israel's military. But beekeepers have returned to areas near the Yellow Line that divides the territory and found enough hives to restart honey production. Producers in Gaza City and parts of Jabalia near the line are now maintaining hives to try and provide some income for themselves and their families. Yet they say their efforts are constrained by Israel's blockade on many items from entering the strip, including ones used for beekeeping. “The bee sector is an important sector for sustainability, ecological balance and farming,” said Ibrahim al-Dabbeh, the head of the Cooperative Association of Beekeepers. Story by The Associated Press CONSUMER Many families will have a fairly long shopping list for school supplies with school back in session, but if you head to stores without a strategy, supply costs can add up fast. WATCH — Consumer reporter Marie Coronel shares practical tips to help families stick to their budget while still picking up those essential school supplies: WE FOLLOW THROUGH Two years after a devastating fire destroyed her San Marcos home and claimed the life of her son, Opal Jean Thompson is finally moving back in. While rebuilding the house brought a fresh start, Thompson says returning home without her son will be the hardest part of all. Still, she’s determined to move forward and make the home feel joyful again. WATCH — After unimaginable loss, Thompson opens the door to her rebuilt home for the first time and shares the emotional journey of starting over: Thanks for waking up with us! item.title: The Man Who Saw AI Coming
item.description:
Source: Annie Lowrey | The Atlantic Score: 5.71
More than a decade ago, the economist Erik Brynjolfsson made a prediction: AI would change everything. Humans began using tools millions of years ago. They cultivated grain and domesticated animals, and then developed written languages, iron tools, the printing press, gunpowder. Progress was slow and local until the mid-1700s, when modern society roared into being alongside machines and engines. Invention built on invention. Then, in recent decades, the pace of human progress slowed again. Productivity growth, the academic measure of how much better people are getting at generating outputs from inputs, collapsed. “We are at a technological plateau,” in the midst of a “great stagnation,” the public intellectual Tyler Cowen argued in 2010. “Apart from the seemingly magical internet, life in broad material terms isn’t so different from what it was in 1953.” Shortly after, the economist Robert Gordon of Northwestern University released a best seller arguing that our era of unprecedented growth and life-changing innovation had come to an end. Cowen and Gordon had the numbers on their side, but Brynjolfsson thought they were wrong. Along with the economist Andrew McAfee, he published two books arguing that the digital revolution was just getting started. AI was already besting human beings at cognitive tasks. Soon, it would make self-driving cars and hyper-smart computers look like nothing more than “warm-up acts,” the pair wrote in The Second Machine Age. Productivity growth would pick up, Brynjolfsson believed. Living standards would improve. Another new society would roar into being. Last month, I visited Brynjolfsson at Stanford, where he teaches, with a few questions in mind: How had he known what AI would be capable of years before the release of ChatGPT and Claude Code?
