For instance, Amazon Prime subscribers in the U.S. can get RxPass, which offers savings on numerous prescription medications for $5 a month, as well as discounted healthcare via One Medical, which is available for an additional $6 a month ($9 for non-subscribers). People in Canada don't have these benefits, although they do have universal healthcare, so arguably don't need them. Meanwhile, the lineups of movies, shows, and channels available through Amazon Prime Video differ between countries due to local broadcasting rights and licensing deals. You want to watch NHL games every Wednesday? You can do that through Amazon Prime Video, but only if you live in Canada, or use a VPN to stream the content. Amazon Prime shipping benefits are (mostly) region-locked Virtually every online shopping platform requires a membership. However, if you know how to game certain systems, you can purchase items unavailable in your region. For instance, you can create a Japanese Nintendo account to purchase digital Switch games exclusive to Japan. However, the same isn't true when buying physical items through Amazon. Many benefits that come with an Amazon Prime subscription are exclusive to their respective countries, most notably free shipping. You can use Amazon Global to purchase items only available on Amazon Canada and ship them to your house in the U.S. (or vice versa), but unless the order meets requirements such as exceeding cash amounts, you won't qualify for free shipping even with Amazon Prime. Given this limitation of Amazon Global, you might wonder if you can save money on shipping if you have multiple Amazon Prime accounts — one for your home country, and one for the country you're ordering from. The answer is no since the benefits only apply to items bought in a country's respective Amazon store and shipped to a local address. Then again, if you have friends or family in Canada and frequently buy gifts for them, you can use an Amazon Prime Canada subscription to save on shipping, but only for these purchases. Otherwise, an Amazon Prime account for the US and another for Canada is a waste of money.

item.title: How Much Solar Power Does Your Home Need To Go Completely Off-Grid?
item.description:
Source: BGR Score: 5.07
How Much Solar Power Does Your Home Need To Go Completely Off-Grid? Solar power is becoming increasingly ubiquitous, though it remains the kind of technology that new consumers have a bevy of questions about. Alongside other things you'll need to know when installing solar, one of the most important considerations is how much electricity you'll need to generate for your home to completely stop relying on the grid for power. The answer, of course, depends on a number of variables, including things like your energy consumption, and the type and efficiency of your solar panels. Your home's location and the amount of sunlight it receives are also factors, which can vary dramatically based on season). That said, it's possible to find some estimates based on averages for the typical American household, and also to directly measure your home's power usage, as well as the likely "energy income" your panels will generate. Another important element of your setup is battery storage, to ensure that you'll have enough power in reserve to cover your needs on overcast days or during shortages and usage spikes. To shave your power bill even further, you could also consider installing some of these extra solar-powered gadgets. Calculating your energy needs According to the U.S. Energy Information Administration (EIA), the average U.S. household uses roughly 10,500 kilowatt-hours (kWh) of electricity every year, which breaks down to 875 kWh a month or 28.8 kWh a day. You can find your personal energy usage by checking your power bill (look for a section labeled "Usage," "Electricity Consumption," or "kWh" on your monthly statement), or by checking your meter (note the number today, wait 30 days, and subtract your starting reading from the new reading to find your total monthly usage). Next, you'll need to figure out how much energy an individual solar panel will generate. A simple way to estimate it is to multiply the panel wattage by the average peak sun hours and multiply that by the system efficiency. For example, a 400W panel in a location with 4.5 peak sun hours and 80% efficiency would result in the following equation: 400 × 4.5 × 0.8 = 1,440 Wh. That equates to 1.44 kWh per day. To discover how many peak sun hours your location receives, check a peak sun hours calculator. You can also make use of a solar calculator. Finally, divide the energy usage of your household by the output of an individual panel to determine the number of panels you'll likely need to supply your home. Going slightly over will always be preferable to being under your required output and finding yourself regularly coming up short and having to rely on the grid to bridge the gap, hence the 20% rule when installing solar.

item.title: These Apps Can Help Track Your Mileage On Waze - Here's How
item.description:
Source: BGR Score: 5.01
These Apps Can Help Track Your Mileage On Waze - Here's How Launched in 2009, Waze is a free, crowd-sourced driving navigation app owned by Google that relies on real-time data provided by drivers for information on road hazards, traffic conditions, and other useful updates. But while Waze is considered by experts to be one of the best navigation apps around, and better than Google Maps for many reasons, some users dislike Waze due to factors such as its limited offline functionality, distracting alerts, background data collection, and inability to automatically track mileage. While Waze can track your driving mileage, it requires users to have the Waze app open, and doesn't allow you to distinguish between personal and business miles — which is important for those who need to track business miles for IRS mileage expense records. However, there are several free apps that work — or integrate directly with — Waze, allowing you to automatically track the mileage of your work and personal journeys. Does Waze tell you how many miles you've driven? Waze can track your mileage in the background, but you need to have the app open and running for it to do so. In addition, to actually see your mileage, you need to open your Waze account's dashboard, which allows you to view your personal information and statistics, including how many Waze Points you've earned. On the dashboard, you'll find your mileage statistics under the 'My Driving Stats' section. This section features a 'Driven Miles' figure, which tells you the number of miles you've driven with the app open. It also tells you your 'Paved Miles,' the distance you've driven using the app's 'Pave road' function, and 'Munched Feet,' which is the distance you've driven on unconfirmed roads. However, this 'Driven Miles' figure is all-encompassing, showing you the overall miles or kilometers you've driven with the Waze app open, and therefore doesn't distinguish between individual journeys or whether a trip was personal or business. As such, it can't store or generate the supporting mileage expense records required by the IRS for deductions and reimbursements. Fortunately, there are free apps that work with Waze that can help track your mileage, and even allow you to create separate reports for business mileage. Apps that can track your Waze mileage AutoMiles is a completely free mileage tracking app that lets you log and categorize every drive (business, commute or personal), without limiting your number of trips or requiring a subscription fee. You can also export your mileage log and GPS routes for your own records or IRS purposes. Everlance is another option that's particularly useful for freelancers and small business owners, as it automatically tracks your mileage and categorizes your trips, with users able to download IRS-compliant mileage logs. This app also works as a general expense tracker, allowing you to upload receipts and input expenses for inclusion in your IRS-ready report. While Everlance's free plan lets you automatically track 30 trips a month, a paid subscription is needed to access reports, and unlimited automatic tracking, with prices starting at $10.99 a month. Neither of these apps integrate directly with Waze, but can run alongside it in the background. If you want an app that integrates with Waze, MileageWise may be a better alternative, as it allows you to navigate with Waze while simultaneously recording your mileage. To do this, open MileageWise and select 'Add new trip,' then select 'Pre-save & Navigate with Waze' from the options menu. When you arrive at your destination, Waze notifies MileageWise, and the latter records the mileage for that journey — which you can then categorize. MileageWise isn't entirely free, but offers a 14-day free trial before users require a subscription — with a yearly subscription starting from $222.22.

item.title: 5 Iconic Android Phones That Made Smartphone History
item.description:
Source: BGR Score: 4.99
5 Iconic Android Phones That Made Smartphone History When Steve Jobs unveiled the iPhone at Macworld in 2007, Android was just a small phone software project Google had purchased, as far as the market was concerned. While Apple's device was the catalyst that started the touchscreen smartphone movement, a diverse array of phone manufacturers were soon hot on the iPhone's heels, and most of them have been powered by Google's Android. While many Android phones have been launched over the years, a few key models played an important role in helping the Android ecosystem grow to where it is today. The very first Android phone released to the public was the HTC Dream, though it included a slide-up keyboard and buttons to help control the device. The iPhone, meanwhile, stood out with a large touchscreen and just a few buttons for power, volume, and the home screen. It wasn't until the Motorola Droid was released in 2009 that Android really hit the mainstream. We looked through the archives to identify which Android phones really left a mark on the industry, and what role they each played. Below is our list, including what helped them stand out and how they pushed Android into the powerhouse software it is today. HTC Dream (T-Mobile G1) The T-Mobile G1, also known as the HTC Dream, was the first commercially released Android phone when it launched in 2008, more than a year after the iPhone landed on store shelves. HTC's device shipped with the Android Market, which is now known as Google Play. The G1 had an interesting start to life, as the phone's initial model, which was codenamed "Sooner," looked similar to a BlackBerry when it was prototyped in 2007. The design was abandoned after the iPhone started making waves, and the new model was marketed as the T-Mobile G1. The phone featured a full physical QWERTY keyboard that appeared when the screen was slid upward. The screen itself was a 3.2-inch TFT capacitive touchscreen at 320x480 resolution. The device also featured five buttons at the bottom of the screen, a clickable trackball, and a 3.15MP camera with autofocus. It wasn't the best-looking model on the market at the time, but the main differentiator was the new Android software that featured three customizable home screens, widgets, and the ability to copy-paste. The addition of a notifications drawer was also seen as a key improvement over the iPhone's experience. Apple adopted a "notification center" in 2011. Motorola Droid The Motorola Droid is one of our top picks for phones that made Android history, because this was a device that truly popularized the Android OS. The Droid was Verizon's answer to the AT&T exclusive iPhone, and is widely considered to be the phone that made Android a consumer brand. Verizon pushed hard to ensure the phone's success too, even licensing the Droid name from Star Wars maker Lucasfilm. Verizon put heavy marketing behind the Motorola Droid, and did the same for a few other models from HTC and Samsung that also used the Droid moniker over the years. The Motorola Droid shipped with a touchscreen and slide-out keyboard similar to the one seen on the T-Mobile G1. It launched with Android 2 and featured turn-by-turn navigation that was considered to be a major differentiator, as the iPhone only had basic navigation instructions at the time. Verizon's ad campaign did its job, with the Droid selling 250,000 units in the first week after its release, which in 2009 was quite a considerable feat. The device reached an estimated 1.2 million unit sales by the fourth quarter of Motorola's 2009 financial year, and set Android on the path to even more popularity. Samsung Galaxy Note You can't discuss Android's greatest hits without including Samsung as part of the conversation. The Samsung Galaxy Note was a device that broke the mold on smartphone form factors, and even though its screen size was considered ludicrously large at the time, its 5.3-inch span is now considered pretty standard. In many ways, the Galaxy Note helped popularize the "phablet" category, further blurring the line between a phone and tablet. It set the bar for larger screens to the point where many smartphone manufacturers have models in each lineup that exceed that size today. The Galaxy Note also revitalized the use of a stylus, Apple had actively shunned with the iPhone. The S Pen received good reviews and proved to be a great productivity tool. The phone shipped with a capable 8MP camera that was able to record 1080p video. It sold more than 10 million units in the nine months after release, proving a commercial success for Samsung. The Note eventually became a key Samsung flagship, though the Note 7 went through dramatic recalls in 2016 due to its tendency to catch fire, making it one of the worst Samsung phones of all time. Samsung stopped making the Galaxy Note in 2021, after the Galaxy Note 20. LG G4 The LG G4 was a moment of brilliance in LG's phone-making era, with screen quality and a camera that set a new bar for what Android smartphones were capable of after its launch in 2015. LG's improvements pushed other Android manufacturers to improve their photography game after some reviewers said the G4's screen and camera could match and surpass the iPhone 6 Plus. The G4 featured a 538 ppi density IPS LCD screen compared to the roughly 401 ppi screen on the iPhone 6 Plus. LG's G4 also had a 16MP, f1.8 camera that received praise for its color accuracy and overall quality. The G4's camera featured optic image stabilization on the X, Y, and Z-axes, and when paired with the laser autofocus and color spectrum sensor, it took amazing photos, even in darker conditions. The G4 also had great video capability, shooting 4K video at 30fps. While LG created an amazing phone in the G4, the company stopped making smartphones in 2021, after a series of profit-bleeding years. Google Pixel The Google Pixel was the first device that saw the tech giant take full control over the hardware and software stack. Launched in 2016, it came after years of Google partnering with other companies to build co-branded Nexus devices. Google set out to make a splash too, creating new features for its Pixel devices, including exclusive usage of the Google Assistant for months before it was released to other Android models. Pixel was pitched as Google's opportunity to showcase Android's potential to the fullest. To do that, Google improved the UI to focus on the company's apps and features. The device also came with unlimited cloud storage via Google Photos. The Pixel's strong point was its camera. Where the LG G4 won in terms of its camera hardware in 2015, the Pixel had even better quality because of its software. Google has kept focus on photography since then as well. Its most recently launched Pixel 10 was considered the iPhone for Android users when it launched in 2025, and particularly got praise for its improved cameras. How we chose our top 5 We looked through the archives to find five devices that had the biggest impact on the industry, and set benchmarks for Android phones that followed them. While there are many Android devices out there that have been favorably reviewed and feature great specs, we focused on devices that truly made a mark and set Android on the path to the market dominance it enjoys today. Honorable mentions should go to the Samsung Galaxy Note Edge with its innovative curved display, and the Samsung Galaxy Fold that helped kick off the modern-day foldable smartphone category. We also couldn't forget the Huawei range of smartphones, which briefly overtook Samsung's worldwide smartphone sales in 2020 before U.S. restrictions stifled its business outside of China. The innovation and diversity these phones have brought to the market have helped Android grow to over 3.8 billion active users, according to Business of Apps. That translates to 73% market share globally, Counterpoint Research said, which means that roughly three-quarters of all smartphones on the planet run on Android.

item.title: Every Nintendo Home Console Released In Chronological Order
item.description:
Source: BGR Score: 4.93
Every Nintendo Home Console Released In Chronological Order Nintendo is one of the most legendary video game companies of all time, enjoying a stellar run in the industry after helping save the medium from the brink of extinction. It has never looked back since, riding on the coattails of iconic video game characters like everyone's favorite plumber to craft incredible gaming experiences. Its unerring focus on unique hardware and software has helped Nintendo reach major heights with its home console offerings every gaming generation — well, bar one. Fans have fond memories of trying to save the princess in "Super Mario Bros.," going on an adventure for the ages in "A Link to the Past," mowing down foes in space as Fox McCloud, enjoying Samus' adventures in first-person, and playing a game of "Wii Sports" with their friends. None of these experiences would've been possible if they didn't find a home on Nintendo's hardware lineup, with their home consoles either invoking feelings of nostalgia or wowing fans with their hybrid design. Color TV-Game Most people think of the NES when talking about Nintendo's first console, but the company had already tried to break into the gaming industry from the very first gaming generation. Well before Atari released a product in the market, and the Magnavox Odyssey was the only way to game at home in the West, Nintendo had released the Color TV-Game series on June 1, 1977. Despite its Japan-only release and the ability to only play a single game with each version of this device, the Color TV-Game series became the highest-selling home console of the first generation, with sales reaching three million. The games that players could check out on these consoles included a racing game with a bird's-eye view, "Computer Othello," a block-breaking game like "Breakout," and "Light Tennis" — Nintendo's version of the classic "Pong." Since Nintendo lacked any experience in console development before this point, it partnered with Mitsubishi Electronics to bring the Color TV-Game to life. Despite the system initially selling at a loss, Nintendo clearly saw something in this console and made enough Color TV-Game systems that they decided to bet on the home console market for the long haul. Nintendo Entertainment System/Famicom A legendary console that needs no introduction, the NES was released in Japan first on July 15, 1983, surviving a buggy launch to become one of the most in-demand gaming platforms in the country. However, as great as Nintendo's domestic success was, they still wanted to break into the Western video game market. Unfortunately, in the same year that this console was released, the video game market had crashed, with Atari attaining a level of market saturation that caused people to turn their noses up at home console hardware. To circumvent this problem, the Famicom — short for "Family Computer" — was rebranded as the Nintendo Entertainment System. This was the first step in a masterstroke gaming strategy that aimed to re-market their product as a toy instead of a console. That helped the console distance itself from the gaming computer moniker that could've injured sales. Two years later, the NES came to Western shores in 1985. With a lineup of strong games that included "Donkey Kong" and "Super Mario Bros.," the focus on quality control and stellar video game experiences helped make home consoles viable outside of Japan once again. An iconic and adored controller design, a game library with over 500 quality titles, and the focus on uniquely weird '80s gaming peripherals and gadgets like the NES Zapper and R.O.B.; these all helped the NES stand out as one of the most legendary gaming consoles ever made. Super Nintendo Entertainment System/Super Famicom Now that Nintendo had proven that the worldwide market would welcome home consoles again, it was time to release an upgraded version of its console. On November 21, 1990, its answer arrived in the form of the Super Famicom in Japan; followed by the U.S. release of the renamed Super Nintendo Entertainment System on August 23, 1991. The 16-bit era of gaming allowed for more detailed visuals, and the SNES made the most of it with incredible games like "Super Mario World," "Final Fantasy VI" (released as "Final Fantasy III" outside of Japan), "Super Metroid," "The Legend of Zelda: A Link to the Past," "Star Fox," "F-Zero," "Chrono Trigger," and "Super Mario Kart." Initially, the SNES' sales trailed behind the Sega Genesis, which ironically enough came into being after the Nintendo NES proved that the console market was ripe for the picking. The SNES eventually overtook its competitor and sold almost 50 million units. The console features stereo sound, more memory, and larger Game Paks to let developers craft wondrous adventures that players could enjoy. The controller's design was also improved, using a dogbone-esque design for greater comfort, and adding two new buttons to let games experiment with slightly more complex control schemes. Given the current trend of loading advanced controllers with as many buttons as possible, it's amusing in hindsight. Nintendo 64 The Nintendo 64 launched on June 23, 1996, with the name stemming from the 64-bit processor it used to usher in a new era of gaming. Known as Project Reality during its development period, Nintendo went all out to create a console that let players enjoy the wonders of 3D gaming. Sega struggled in this department, with "Sonic Adventure" serving as a fitting example of how its IP failed to make a proper transition to 3D. The brilliance of "Super Mario 64" highlighted that Nintendo was a champ when it came to both home console and video game development. However, as great as the console's video game library was, the N64 struggled on two fronts: Firstly, the console stuck to cartridges instead of switching over to CD technology, causing many third-party developers to move on from this console to PlayStation. Speaking of which, the debut of Sony's first gaming console, which happened after Nintendo refused to partner with Sony on a console that used CD-ROMs, was another hurdle that the N64 failed to overcome. The PlayStation was marketed to children and adults alike, with its hardware surpassing anything the N64 had to offer. As a result, Nintendo technically won its battle with Sega, only for Sony to swoop in and win the fifth-generation console war. Nintendo GameCube Despite the N64 falling well behind in sales as compared to the PlayStation, Nintendo's priority wasn't to release a system with amazing hardware that let players enjoy state-of-the-art 3D visuals. Their focus was on crafting quality video games, and the GameCube added another layer to the mix with its quirky looks. The iconic purple color of the GameCube is easily identifiable. Even the controller had an in-your-face design, using the best lessons learned from Sony's amazing PS1 controllers while adding a trademark Nintendo flair. The games released on this console following its launch on September 14, 2001 are certainly legendary in their own right, with beloved titles like "Super Smash Bros. Melee," "The Legend of Zelda: The Wind Waker," and "Metroid Prime" being standout highlights. Still, despite being the complete package, including the switch to optical media, the sales of the GameCube were still disappointing. The legend Shigeru Miyamoto himself has gone on record to state that the Nintendo GameCube failed. It became increasingly clear that the PlayStation had eaten into Nintendo's consumer base extensively, and a massive paradigm shift needed to be carried out if the company still wanted to remain in the console business. Wii The N64 and GameCube hadn't exactly been barn-burners in terms of sales. Realizing that Sony and Microsoft were now at war with each other and trying to capture the hardcore gaming market, Nintendo let each other fight this battle without getting involved. Instead, Nintendo decided to market an accessible home console for the entire family; to the point where the controller developed for the Wii resembled a regular TV remote. Nintendo emphasized motion controls in this console, going the extra mile to ensure that this immersive control mode would be carried out without a hitch by utilizing a sensor bar that used IR signals to read the Wiimote's motion. The end result is the Nintendo Wii, the ultimate party console that gamers across multiple generations could play. It helped that titles like "Wii Sports," "Wii Play," and "Wii Fit" had little to no barriers to entry, becoming genuine pick-up-and-play experiences that further enhanced the Wii's appeal to all folks. As a result, the Wii sold more than 100 million units since its launch on November 19, 2006, becoming the seventh-highest-selling video game console of all time. If you missed out on this console's golden years, why not buy an old Nintendo Wii for cheap to enjoy a fun party night with your friends? Wii U The Wii was a smash hit, and all Nintendo had to do was carry forward this momentum with the launch of its successor, codenamed Project Cafe. However, while the success of the Wii encouraged Nintendo to take some risks, the company went way overboard in this department, leading to one of the weirdest products ever made by Nintendo. This could be sensed from the very moment the Wii U was announced with its bulky controller (the heaviest ever released for a home console), alongside disappointing hardware specs. The Wii U became Nintendo's lowest-selling home console of all time. The controller was very unwieldy because of its weight, and it didn't help that the battery life was also woeful. Compared to the simple Wiimote that appealed to casuals, the interface of the Wii U's gamepad felt rather complex in comparison. Even with the 1080p visuals and a brief lead over its competition, the Wii U was a massive failure and barely reached 14 million units in lifetime sales after launching on November 18, 2012. If it wasn't for the Nintendo 3DS handheld keeping the company afloat, chances are that Nintendo would've had to shutter its console division outright. Nintendo Switch Nintendo needed a home run after the Wii U's failure. It could've been very easy for them to play it safe and provide a console offering in the same vein as Sony or Microsoft, but the need to innovate is what made Nintendo such a beloved brand in the first place. So, with the Nintendo Switch, the company decided to merge both handheld and home console into one package. Before the Nintendo Switch, no console maker had proposed the idea of a hybrid console that could work on both an external display and by itself. With the inclusion of a dock, detachable Joy-Con controllers (innovative despite their poor build quality), and impressive third-party support, the Nintendo Switch regained a dominant position in the gaming industry previously lost by the Wii U. It helped that Nintendo launched this console on March 3, 2017, along with "The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild," which is easily one of the greatest open-world adventure games ever made. "Super Mario Odyssey" was released in the same year, and became one of the best 3D platformers in recent memory. People who only wanted a handheld version of this device could opt for the cheaper Nintendo Switch Lite, while others who didn't mind paying a premium could get the more expensive OLED display model. Nintendo Switch 2 For Nintendo, the current gaming generation started on June 5, 2025, with the launch of the Nintendo Switch 2. Instead of making the same mistake as the Wii U, Nintendo clearly adopted an "if it ain't broke, don't fix it" mentality. The form factor is largely similar, with the Switch 2 operating in a similar manner to the previous console. The Nintendo Switch 2 retains its hybrid functionality and bolsters the Switch's hardware to the point where it can outperform the PS4 when docked, which is no mean feat. Support for backwards compatibility with all games for the original Switch is also much welcome, incentivizing you to transfer your games to the Switch 2 from your old console. Now, with the whole physical media debacle marring PlayStation's name, it's understandable why some gamers would want to switch allegiances to maintain their integrity. Joy-Cons have arguably seen the biggest improvement over the original Switch. Instead of the slide-and-click attachment that most people are used to, it uses magnets as a far more refined and simple solution to attach on the Switch 2. It even comes with a mouse mode, courtesy of an optical sensor, that will make playing simulation and strategy titles far simpler on Switch 2. It even supports 4K resolutions in docked mode, which is genuinely impressive. Unlike the Switch, its successor hasn't exactly launched with a variety of amazing games, although titles like "Donkey Kong Bananza," "Mario Kart World," and "Pokemon Pokopia" are slowly but surely bolstering the Switch 2's game library.

item.title: The Best Store-Bought Pasta Sauce, Tested and Reviewed (2026)
item.description:
Source: Bon Appétit Score: 5.37
The best jarred marinara starts with, you guessed it, bright tomato flavor, balanced acidity, a hint of sweetness, and herbs that add complexity without stealing the show. Unfortunately, not every red sauce in the pasta aisle gets there. Some were oddly sweet, others tasted of ancient herbs recovered from the pantry of your last Airbnb, and a few were so smooth they bordered on soup. After tasting 17 nationally available marinara sauces, Bon Appétit editors named Bertolli the best overall and best for pasta, Rao’s the best for pizza, and Mezzetta the best for dipping. Our favorite marinara: Bertolli Bertolli Traditional Marinara won the top spot for marinara sauce for its rich tomato flavor and pleasantly chunky texture. With its zing of acidity and bright red color (no sad desaturated sauce allowed here), we declared this the best marinara for livening up any pasta. Why it won us over: As our editors tasted through the contenders, they found many marinaras to be over-blended and watery. Not so with Bertolli, which contained generous chunks of tomato in varying sizes, making every bite dynamic. That texture was complemented by balanced sweetness and acidity and a zingy punch of garlic. Best for: any pasta dish that requires a tomato sauce—think Chris’s Easiest Meatballs, or a tomato-y bucatini with tomato and chili. The best marinara for pizza: Rao’s While chunky marinara is best for pasta, pizzas benefit from a smoother sauce. Rao’s Homemade Marinara delivered exactly that, plus robust flavor, which is why our editors declared this jar the ideal store-bought marinara for homemade pizza. Why it won us over: Rao’s marinara is more silky smooth than chunky, but that’s exactly why it works as a pizza sauce. What really won over our editors were the brand’s deft use of herbs and other aromatics: Notes of oregano and anise tickled our tasters’ taste buds, while a sturdy backbone of roasted garlic kept the flavor grounded. Some editors found Rao’s close to the edge of too salty—enough to overdo it when tossed with well-seasoned noodles (you are salting your pasta water, aren’t you?). On pizza, though, that assertiveness will meld nicely with the crust below. Best for: generously ladling onto pizza dough before baking, or dolloping liberally over the top of Double-Tomato Focaccia. The best marinara for dipping: Mezzetta For dipping, we wanted a marinara that was fresh and flavorful right out of the jar, no heating required. (Scandalous, we know!) Mezzetta Family Co. Marinara, with its robust hit of fresh basil, fit the bill. Why it won us over: While some contenders stood out for their herbs in a bad way, Mezzetta tasted like a freshly plucked sprig of basil had found its way into the sauce just before jarring. The lively herbs and rich tomato flavor—slightly sweet as if it had been caramelized—made this sauce delicious even at room temperature. Some editors even said they’d have no problem popping the top and pouring it straight into a ramekin for dipping. Best for: homemade mozzarella sticks, or simply as a dip for tortilla chips. How we tested Tasters assembled in the Test Kitchen to sample each marinara, from anonymized ramekins, before rating and reviewing. We tasted each sauce plain so the tomatoes, herbs, seasoning, and texture had nowhere to hide. After narrowing the contenders to our five favorites, we discussed the finalists in terms of their ideal applications, finally settling on our top three premade marinara sauces. What we looked for Bright tomato flavor was nonnegotiable, but it wasn’t enough on its own. Texture matters too: We wanted sauces that felt like tomatoes, not tomato purée. We favored sauces with balanced acidity and a cohesive texture, while watery, grainy, or separated sauces quickly fell out of contention. What became clear as we tasted was that there isn’t one perfect marinara for every use, so we crowned winners for pasta, pizza, and dipping instead. - 365 Organic Marinara Sauce: A mellow oregano-forward flavor and somewhat watery texture. - Barilla Premium Marinara: Overpowered by dried basil, which masked the tomato flavor. - Carbone Marinara: Visible oil separation made the texture feel less cohesive than our favorites. - Cento Marinara Pasta Sauce: A pronounced sour aftertaste kept this one out of the running. - Good & Gather Marinara: Bright and well-balanced with a velvety texture, but ultimately edged out by stronger contenders. - Great Value Marinara: Slightly sweet with an unexpectedly woodsy, almost cinnamon-like finish. - Kirkland Signature Organic Tuscan Marinara: Chunky with bright basil notes, but lacking the concentrated tomato flavor we were looking for. - Mutti Marinara: A distinct cheesiness muted the tomato flavor and made it feel less versatile. - Newman’s Own Marinara: Thinner and sweeter than our ideal. - Prego Traditional Marinara: Too sweet for most of our tasters. - Ragú Old World Style Marinara: Mild and approachable, but too subdued, with little herbal complexity. - Safeway Signature Select Marinara: Noticeably sweet and watery, though several tasters thought it could improve with garlic, herbs, and a longer simmer. - San Merican Sugo di Pomodoro: Another sauce whose cheesy notes distracted from the tomatoes. - Trader Joe’s Organic Marinara: Good consistency, but heavy oregano and a slightly soapy flavor profile held it back.

item.title: Whiskey Sour
item.description:
Source: Bon Appétit Score: 5.19
A classic whiskey sour is one of the easiest classic cocktails to master. Made with bourbon, fresh lemon juice, simple syrup, and the occasional egg white, the drink delivers a perfect balance of sweet, tart, and boozy. It’s just as fitting for happy hour as it is for holiday gatherings. The best whiskey sour recipes hinge on freshly squeezed lemon juice and shaking the cocktail well with plenty of ice until thoroughly chilled. Fresh citrus gives the drink its bright, refreshing flavor, while bourbon adds notes of vanilla, caramel, and spice. Serve over fresh ice with an orange wheel and a cocktail cherry for the classic finishing touch. Whiskey Sour FAQs Shouldn’t a whiskey sour have egg white? It’s up to you. Egg white gives a whiskey sour a silkier texture and foamy top, but it also softens the drink’s bright citrus flavor. If you’d like to use it, add one egg white for every two cocktails and dry shake (shake all the ingredients before adding ice), then shake again over ice. Editor’s note: Raw egg is not recommended for infants, the elderly, pregnant women, people with weakened immune systems...or people who don’t like raw eggs. What’s the best bourbon for a whiskey sour? A balanced, approachable bourbon works best in a whiskey sour. In Bon Appétit’s bourbon taste test, Bulleit Bourbon stood out as an especially good choice for whiskey sours thanks to its caramel, vanilla, and peppery notes. Buffalo Trace, Four Roses, Elijah Craig, and Wild Turkey 101 are also solid options if you prefer a different style. Can I make a whiskey sour without simple syrup? Simple syrup is the easiest sweetener because it dissolves instantly in your shaker, but you can also use maple syrup or honey thinned with an equal portion of water. Each will give the cocktail a slightly different flavor. For the easiest simple syrup, combine equal parts cold water and granulated sugar in a blender and blend on high until the sugar is dissolved. Store leftover syrup in the refrigerator for about 2 weeks. What’s the difference between a whiskey sour and a New York Sour? Recipe information - Total Time 2 minutes - Yield Makes 1 Ingredients 2 ¾ ¾ ½ Need to make a substitution? Preparation - Step 1Combine 2 oz. bourbon, ¾ oz. fresh lemon juice, and ¾ oz. simple syrup in a cocktail shaker filled with ice. Cover and shake vigorously until outside of shaker is very cold, about 20 seconds. Step 2Strain cocktail through a Hawthorne strainer or a slotted spoon into an old-fashioned or rocks glass filled with fresh ice. Garnish with ½ orange wheel and a maraschino cherry threaded onto a cocktail pick. Editor’s note: This whiskey sour recipe was first printed in our May 2016 issue; it has been updated for style. Head this way for more of our best bourbon cocktails →

item.title: Artichoke Beurre
item.description:
Source: Bon Appétit Score: 5.00
It’s That Simple is our series about recipes so easy, you can make them with your eyes closed. Think tiny ingredient lists, laid-back techniques, and results so delicious you’ll text home about them. Also known as le Parisien, a jambon-beurre sandwich is as simple as it gets. A fresh baguette, ruffles of salty ham, and a layer of butter so thick that, when you bite into it, teeth marks are left behind (sometimes also a swipe of Dijon mustard or scattering of sliced cornichons or both is added). This is an audacious vegetarian version—which is to say, entirely untraditional and a little unhinged. Instead of ham, there are jarred marinated artichokes (don’t toss the marinade). These have a meaty texture and inherent umami, which is only accented by a quick trip under the broiler. The rest of the sandwich stays true to the classic. It’s pantry-friendly and picnic-ready, as welcome for a chic desk lunch as it is for a day in the sun. Recipe information - Total Time 10 minutes - Yield 1–2 servings Ingredients 1 1 4 10 6 Need to make a substitution? Preparation - Heat broiler (place a rack in upper third if your broiler is in your oven). If your bread is soft, place one 10–12" demi baguette, halved lengthwise, cut side down, on a rimmed baking sheet and broil until lightly crisped (do not let it brown; if baguette is fresh from a bakery, no need to broil). Drain one 12-oz. jar marinated quartered artichoke hearts. Coarsely chop about half of artichokes and arrange all artichokes on a rimmed baking sheet (use the same one if you crisped the bread). Broil, checking often, until edges start to char, 5–10 minutes, depending on your broiler. Smear 4 Tbsp. salted European butter, thinly sliced, over top half of bread. Evenly arrange 10 cornichons, very thinly sliced lengthwise, and, if there are cocktail onions in the jar, about 6 cocktail onions, halved, over butter, gently pressing to adhere. Slather bottom half of bread with Dijon mustard, then top with broiled artichokes. Close up sandwich and cut in half.

item.title: Mango Chicken Summer Rolls
item.description:
Source: Bon Appétit Score: 4.93
Conveniently made with shredded rotisserie chicken, these no-cook, fresh summer rolls are a delightful lunch or dinner, especially on sticky summer days. If you’re feeding a crowd, double the ingredients and set it all up as a DIY summer roll bar, with each person in charge of filling and rolling their own chubby cylinder of crunchy vegetables and spicy chicken. The rice papers need only a brief dip in cool (never warm) water. You want them coated in a film of water but not sodden. They’ll continue to soften and flex as you fill and roll. Serve these summer rolls immediately after filling. Too hot to go near a stove? Check out more of these no-cook recipes: Smashed Zucchini With Tahini-Ginger Dressing; Stone Fruit and Salami Panzanella; and Spicy Tuna Tostadas Recipe information - Total Time 30 minutes - Yield 4 servings Ingredients Sauce ½ 2 2 2 1 1 Rolls and Assembly 2 1 1 12 1 3 1 ½ Need to make a substitution? Preparation - SauceStep 1Whisk ½ cup creamy peanut butter, 2 Tbsp. chili sauce (such as sriracha), 2 Tbsp. distilled white vinegar, 2 Tbsp. oyster sauce, 1 Tbsp. fish sauce, 1 Tbsp. sugar, and ¼ cup water in a medium bowl until smooth and creamy. If sauce is thick, add a few splashes of water to loosen to the consistency of ketchup. - Rolls and AssemblyStep 2Toss 2 cups shredded chicken meat (from about ½ small rotisserie chicken), 1 Tbsp. chili sauce (such as sriracha), 1 Tbsp. oyster sauce, and a pinch of kosher salt in a medium bowl to coat chicken. Step 3Working one at a time, dip twelve 8"-diameter rice papers into a large shallow bowl filled with cool water, just long enough to coat in a film of water (you don’t want them to be floppy). Shake off excess water and place on surface. Place 1 leaf (or 2 if leaves are small) from 1 head of butter lettuce, leaves separated, on bottom third of a paper to act as a cup. Arrange about ¼ cup of 3 cups 2" matchstick crunchy vegetables (such as carrots, radishes, and/or cucumbers), 2 Tbsp. seasoned chicken, a few pieces from 1 large mango, peeled, pitted, cut into 2" matchsticks, and a few pieces from ½ bunch cilantro, tough stems removed, cut into 1" pieces, on top of lettuce. Fold sides of rice paper up and over filling, then starting with the side closest to you, roll up rice paper gently but tightly. Repeat with remaining ingredients to make 11 more rolls. Step 4Lightly coat a platter with vegetable oil and arrange summer rolls on top. Cut in half diagonally if desired and serve with peanut sauce for dipping.

item.title: Palm Springs Date Shake
item.description:
Source: Bon Appétit Score: 4.90
An old-school California date shake is definitely not a smoothie. A specialty of Southern California’s Coachella Valley, where date palms thrive in the desert climate, it’s a rich, sweet milkshake that’s spawned countless iterations made with frozen bananas, almond milk, Greek yogurt, or nut butter. This date shake recipe keeps the focus on the dates and store-bought vanilla ice cream. Pitted Medjool dates give the shake its signature caramel-like sweetness and thick texture, while a pinch of cinnamon brings warmth. Our version also adds tahini for nutty flavor and an extra-silky texture. For the smoothest shake, soak the dates in hot water for 10 minutes before blending and give the ice cubes a few quick pulses to give them a head start. Date Shake FAQ Do I have to soak the dates? Soaking the Medjool dates in hot water for 10 minutes softens them so they break down more easily in the blender. Save the soaking liquid: You’ll add a tablespoon to the shake, plus more as needed to help everything blend smoothly. If you have a high-powered blender, like a Vitamix, you can get away without soaking, but the texture might not be as smooth. Why do you crush the ice before making a date shake? Pulsing the ice cubes a few times in the blender breaks them into smaller pieces before the other ingredients go in, helping them incorporate more easily. Don’t completely pulverize the ice at this stage; pulse just until lightly crushed. Can you make a date shake without a high-speed blender? Yes. A high-speed blender will give you the smoothest results, but soaking the dates and lightly crushing the ice before adding the remaining ingredients will help a standard blender process everything more easily. What kind of dates should I use? Use Medjool dates. They’re soft and plump, with a caramel-like sweetness that works especially well here. Here are our favorites: Recipe information - Total Time 15 minutes - Yield 2 Servings Ingredients 6 1 1 ¼ Need to make a substitution? Preparation - Step 1Place 6 pitted Medjool dates (about 3 oz.), in a small bowl and pour in ½ cup hot water to cover; soak 10 minutes to let soften. Step 2Pulse 8 ice cubes in a blender, preferably high-speed, just to slightly crush ice. Add dates and 1 Tbsp. date soaking liquid, 1 cup vanilla ice cream, 1 Tbsp. (heaping) tahini, ¼ tsp. Diamond Crystal or Morton kosher salt, and a pinch of ground cinnamon and blend, adding more date soaking liquid a tablespoonful at a time if needed to help get things moving, until smooth. Taste shake and season with more salt if needed. Divide between 2 glasses. Editor’s note: This date shake recipe was first printed in our May 2016 issue. Upon retesting in 2026, we found that the ½ cup toasted walnuts in the original version overpowered the dates, giving the shake a bitter edge. We swapped them for tahini, which lends subtler nuttiness and a silkier texture, and reduced the amount of dates from ½ cup for a more balanced sweetness. We now also call for Medjool dates, exclusively, instead of Medjoor or Deglet Noor; Medjool dates tend to be softer and make for a creamier shake. The recipe has been updated accordingly. Head this way for more soda-fountain favorites from our friends at Epicurious →

item.title: Lemon Buttermilk Pie
item.description:
Source: Bon Appétit Score: 4.74
Cookbook author and former Bon Appétit food editor Alison Roman developed this lemon buttermilk pie more than a decade ago, and it remains one of our most-loved pie recipes. Think of it as a brighter, more fragrant take on chess pie, with the tang of buttermilk in both the flaky crust and silky filling. Fresh lemon zest and lemon juice keep the custard vibrant, while just a pinch of saffron adds delicate floral notes and a golden hue without overpowering the citrus. If you’re new to cooking with saffron, a little goes a long way. If you’d rather skip it, the pie will still be delicious. In the crust, buttermilk creates an especially tender, flaky texture. Blind baking is critical to ensure it stays crisp beneath the creamy filling. Handle the dough gently to keep it flaky, and let the finished pie cool completely before serving with softly whipped cream. Lemon Buttermilk Pie FAQ What does buttermilk do in this pie? Can I swap it out? Buttermilk adds a subtle tang that balances the sweetness of the custard. It’s also used in the pie dough, where it helps create a tender, flaky crust. While there are some applications in which it’s easy to substitute buttermilk for a similar ingredient, this isn’t the place. It is a “buttermilk” pie, after all. However, if you absolutely must, plain kefir is an easy 1:1 substitute. Plain whole-milk yogurt thinned with milk until pourable also works. Where did buttermilk pie come from? Buttermilk pie is a classic Southern dessert with roots that stretch back to early American home baking. Like chess pie, it was traditionally made with pantry staples—eggs, sugar, butter, and cultured dairy—making it an affordable dessert that didn’t rely on fresh fruit or expensive ingredients. This version stays true to that creamy custard tradition while adding bright lemon and an optional pinch of saffron. Do I have to use saffron? Recipe information - Yield 8 Servings Ingredients Dough 1¼ 1 ½ ½ ¼ Filling and assembly 2 3 1¼ 1¼ 1 ⅓ ¼ 2 Need to make a substitution? Preparation - DoughStep 1Pulse 1¼ cups (156 g) all-purpose flour, 1 Tbsp. sugar, and ½ tsp. Diamond Crystal or ¼ tsp. Morton kosher salt in a food processor to combine. Add ½ cup (1 stick) chilled unsalted butter, cut into pieces, and pulse until mixture resembles coarse meal with a few pea-size pieces of butter remaining. Step 2Transfer to a large bowl and add ¼ cup buttermilk. Mix with a fork, adding more buttermilk by the tablespoon if needed, just until a shaggy dough comes together; knead very lightly until no dry spots remain. Pat into a disk and wrap in plastic. Chill at least 4 hours. Do Ahead: Dough can be made 2 days ahead. Keep chilled. - Filling and assemblyStep 3Preheat oven to 325°. Roll out pie dough on a lightly floured surface to a 14" round. Transfer to a 9"-diameter pie dish, allowing dough to slump down into dish. Trim dough, leaving about a 1" overhang. Fold overhang under and crimp edges. Prick bottom all over with a fork. Freeze 15 minutes. Step 4Line crust with parchment paper or foil, leaving overhang, and fill with pie weights or dried beans. Place pie dish on a rimmed baking sheet and bake until crust is dry around the edges, 20–25 minutes. Remove parchment and weights and bake until surface looks dry, 10–12 minutes longer. Step 5Meanwhile, blend 3 large eggs plus 6 large egg yolks, 1¼ cups buttermilk, 1¼ cups (250 g) sugar, 1 Tbsp. finely grated lemon zest, ⅓ cup fresh lemon juice, ¼ tsp. Diamond Crystal or Morton kosher salt, and a pinch of saffron threads (if using) in a blender until smooth. With motor running, add 2 Tbsp. all-purpose flour, then 2 Tbsp. unsalted butter, melted, cooled slightly. Tap blender jar against countertop to burst any air bubbles in filling and pour through a fine-mesh sieve into warm crust; discard any solids (some saffron threads might sneak through the strainer; this is fine). Step 6Bake pie, rotating halfway through and covering edges of crust with foil if browning too quickly before filling is done, until filling is set around edges but center still jiggles slightly when gently shaken, 55–65 minutes. Transfer pie to a wire rack and let cool. Serve pie topped with whipped cream. Do Ahead: Pie can be baked 2 days ahead. Keep at room temperature up to 6 hours; cover and chill to hold longer. Editor’s note: This buttermilk pie recipe was first printed in our March 2014 issue; it has been updated for style. Head this way for more of our favorite cream pie recipes →

item.title: Former OpenAI executive Kevin Weil has sought a valuation of at least $750 million for his new AI science startup
item.description:
Source: Business Insider Score: 7.49
Kevin Weil, the former chief product officer of OpenAI, has sought a valuation of at least $750 million for a new AI science startup, in the latest example of AI pushing into science. Weil is aiming to raise $150 million in the round, according to three people with knowledge of the discussions. The details have not been finalized yet and could still change. Weil did not respond to a request for comment. Weil's fundraising is a broader sign that AI's next frontier is shifting from chatbots to science. A growing number of OpenAI and Google alums are launching startups that promise to accelerate scientific discovery, from designing new drugs to running autonomous experiments. Weil departed OpenAI earlier this year, where he was chief product officer and then oversaw science initiatives. He oversaw Prism, a workspace designed to bring frontier models directly into scientists' workflows. Prior to OpenAI, Weil was a product executive at Meta and Twitter. He holds various board seats, including on the boards of Cisco and Stoke Space. The exact details of his new startup could not be learned, but sources say he has pitched it as a way to gather scientific data for AI models. Weil is far from the only senior OpenAI leader to head for the exits. Brad Lightcap, the company's longtime former chief operating officer, announced that he was leaving after eight years to start "something new." Fidji Simo stepped down as CEO of applications in July, citing health reasons, and moved into a part-time advisory role. In April, Weil's departure coincided with the exits of Sora's head, Bill Peebles, and Srinivas Narayanan, OpenAI's CTO for business applications. Weil's new AI-for-science startup enters an increasingly competitive race to use artificial intelligence to automate the scientific process. Periodic Labs, founded by former OpenAI researcher Liam Fedus and former Google DeepMind researcher Ekin Dogus Cubuk, is building AI scientists alongside autonomous laboratories where robots can conduct physical experiments and generate new training data. Investors in that company include Andreessen Horowitz, Accel, Jeff Bezos, and Eric Schmidt. Last week, Jeff Dean, Google's chief scientist, announced that he and three other colleagues were leaving to start Discovery Loop, an AI startup focused on AI applications in science and engineering.

item.title: Airlines and charter companies are selling front-row seats to the solar eclipse for up to $1,200
item.description:
Source: Business Insider Score: 6.18
Some adventurous travelers are skipping the crowds on the ground to watch Wednesday's solar eclipse from thousands of feet in the air, thanks to a handful of specially arranged airline and charter flights. Brussels Airlines is flying 100 people over France to view the partial eclipse, Aerospace Global News reported. The flight, in partnership with the Urania Public Observatory in Switzerland, is sold out. Tickets were about $350 a person. The aisle seats will be left open to give people more space to see out the windows. The four-hour experience will include about two hours in the sky. Seeing the phenomena at altitude above the clouds eliminates some of the obstructions that interfere with viewing it from the ground. The Urania Public Observatory has also partnered with the ASL Group, a European private aviation company, for a solar eclipse flight from Liège, Belgium. A seat on the sold-out private Embraer E135 jet cost about $920 a person. Another private aviation company, UK-based Air Charter Service, charged people about $1,200 to fly them from London to one of three possible viewing locations for the total eclipse: Valladolid or the Balearic Islands in Spain, or Reykjavik, Iceland. Food and drinks, including alcohol, will be served on the round-trip flight, and approved telescope equipment will be allowed onboard. Although not open to the public, Spanish flag carrier Iberia will carry scientists on a special charter flight from Madrid to see the total eclipse over Northern Spain. The flight will be live-streamed on Iberia's social media channels, thanks to the Airbus plane's high-speed Starlink WiFi. Onboard the Iberia flight will be researchers from the Shelios project, an astronomical scientific initiative led by the Spanish astronomer Miquel Serra-Ricart. They will observe the solar corona and surrounding celestial objects, such as Venus and Mercury. For those with previously planned flights on Wednesday and hoping to catch a glimpse of the eclipse, it's possible to see it if the plane happens to be in the right place at the right time and if the sun is visible from their window. Wednesday's total solar eclipse will be visible from the Arctic, Iceland, Greenland, northern Spain, and small areas in Siberia and Portugal. The start time will vary by location, and totality is expected to last up to about 2 minutes and 18 seconds, although it will last less than two minutes in many populated land areas. In North America, a partial eclipse will be visible from parts of Canada, Alaska, and the northern US. The last total solar eclipse in the US was in April 2024, and the next one won't happen again until March 2033, but only in Alaska. The continental US will see its next total eclipse in August 2044.

item.title: Ukrainian troops are buying war robots from their digital marketplace in record numbers
item.description:
Source: Business Insider Score: 5.15
Ukrainian troops are rushing to a digital weapons marketplace to buy record numbers of ground robots, reflecting the surging popularity of these combat machines on the battlefield. Brave1, the Ukrainian state-backed innovation platform, said on Monday that the military has ordered more than 3,000 ground robots from its digital marketplace since it launched last year, including over 640 units in July alone. That latter figure represents a 680% increase over 2025's monthly average, Brave1 said in a statement. Yuliia Myrna, product manager for the Brave1 Market digital site, said in remarks shared with Business Insider that ground robots and interceptor drones "are among the fastest-growing categories we are seeing in 2026." Ukraine launched the Brave1 Market in April 2025, granting soldiers access to an Amazon-style website to buy military technology, such as drones, robots, and electronic warfare systems, from the defense industry, streamlining the procurement process. In October 2025, uncrewed ground vehicles became eligible for purchase with "ePoints," which Ukrainian troops collect for verified kills of Russian soldiers or military hardware, and the completion of other battlefield tasks. Various drone types, including first-person-view (FPV) quadcopters, interceptors, and heavy bombers, are among the most popular items on the Brave1 Market by quantity. While ground robots can cost tens of thousands of dollars — typically making them far more expensive than these other drones — they serve in drastically different roles and have a longer operational lifecycle. Myrna said Ukraine is "deliberately accelerating" the integration of ground robots into combat operations, particularly for logistics and casualty evacuation. "Military units now earn ePoints for successfully completing these missions with robotic systems, creating an incentive to replace personnel in high-risk tasks wherever possible," she said. "This creates a powerful development cycle," Myrna added, explaining that "more battlefield use generates more operational feedback for manufacturers, which leads to faster product improvements and ultimately helps us move people away from missions that can be performed by machines." Only a few Ukrainian companies produced ground robots at the start of Russia's full-scale invasion. Today, there are roughly 280 firms that make hundreds of different products, Andrii Hrytseniuk, Brave1's CEO, told Business Insider. The growing popularity of uncrewed ground vehicles on the Brave1 Market reflects Ukraine's broader push to replace soldiers with robots and drones in dangerous missions, particularly front-line supply runs. Ukrainian officials have said they want robots to handle 100% of battlefield logistics, missions that have become particularly deadly as the "kill zone" — the drone-saturated area that surrounds the front line — continues to expand. Ukrainian commanders told Business Insider that the robots allow their units to perform critical tasks while keeping troops out of harm's way. Grek, a UGV company commander with the 21st Unmanned Systems "Kraken" Regiment, who asked to only be identified by his call sign, said that "the stakes of removing humans from dangerous missions are significant." "Every time a person is exposed to a high-risk environment, there is a possibility of injury, loss of life, or reduced combat effectiveness," he said. "Protecting personnel means preserving experience, training, and leadership that cannot easily be replaced."

item.title: The 10 best places to retire in Florida, ranked
item.description:
Source: Business Insider Score: 5.14
Florida has long been a retirement destination, drawing older Americans with its warm weather, beaches, and historically lower cost of living. In recent years, it has lost some of its appeal as a retirement haven, with some older Americans put off by the Sunshine State's rising housing and homeowners' insurance costs, overdevelopment and congestion, hurricane risks, and intensifying heat. Still, Florida remains one of the country's most popular retirement destinations — and some of its cities offer a better lifestyle for retirees than others. US News & World Report ranked the best places to retire in Florida, evaluating each destination across six categories: quality of life, value, healthcare quality, retiree taxes, senior population and migration, and the job market. The categories were weighted based on a March 2025 survey of 3,500 Americans ages 45 and older, who were asked which factors mattered most when choosing where to retire. The ranking focused on more populous cities with consistent data, so some smaller towns popular with retirees weren't included. The ranking drew on data from the US Census Bureau, the Department of Commerce, the Federal Reserve, the Bureau of Economic Analysis, and various state and local sources. Here are the 10 best places to retire in Florida, ranked from lowest to highest. 10. Jacksonville The largest city included in US News' ranking of the 10 best places to retire in Florida, Jacksonville offers retirees the amenities of a major city while still providing miles of beaches, parks, and waterways. Its size means residents can choose from a number of diverse neighborhoods and access a broad range of dining, entertainment, outdoor recreation, and healthcare options. The median home value is $313,862, the median monthly rent is $1,352, and the median household income is reported at $70,119. 9. Port Charlotte Port Charlotte, located on Charlotte Harbor along Southwest Florida's Gulf Coast, may appeal to retirees seeking a slower pace and easy access to the water. The area, which has a population of over 50,000 residents, offers opportunities for boating, fishing, golfing, and exploring the nearby Gulf Coast beaches. It's also more affordable to live there than other places on this list — the median monthly rent is $1,136, and the median household income is reported at $62,785. 8. Bonita Springs Bonita Springs offers a laid-back Gulf Coast lifestyle with beaches, parks, and opportunities for boating and other outdoor activities. Its location between Naples and Fort Myers also gives retirees convenient access to the shopping, dining, and entertainment in both areas, with an average commute time of 22 minutes. The median home value in Bonita Springs is $518,813, while the median household income is $95,589. 7. Cape Coral With an extensive network of canals, Cape Coral is particularly well-suited to retirees who enjoy living life out on the water. And, with an average commute time of 26 minutes, driving isn't so bad, either. It's one of the most-populated locations on this list, with a population of 222,946. The Gulf Coast city also offers parks, golf courses, and access to nearby beaches and islands, with a median household income of $79,932. 6. Pensacola Pensacola offers retirees white-sand Gulf Coast beaches alongside the amenities and cultural attractions of a historic city. Its waterfront setting and access to fishing, boating, and other outdoor activities can make it especially attractive to retirees who want to stay active while keeping costs low: The median home value here is $320,128, and the median monthly rent is $1,186. 5. Naples Naples is known for its Gulf Coast beaches, golf courses, upscale shopping, and dining scene. Retirees looking for an active coastal lifestyle can spend their time on the water, exploring the city's cultural attractions, or enjoying this coastal city's many exciting outdoor activities. While more expensive than other towns on this list — the median home value sits at $1.4 million — the median household income sits at around $151,000, and the median monthly rent is $1,873. 4. Palm Harbor Palm Harbor combines a suburban atmosphere with easy access to the beaches and attractions of the Tampa Bay area. Retirees can enjoy nearby parks, golf courses, and waterfront activities, as well as the restaurants and shops of its historic downtown. The median home value averages at $414,990, while the median monthly rent is $1,716. 3. Palm Coast Palm Coast may appeal to retirees seeking a relaxed coastal lifestyle with access to beaches, waterways, and nature preserves. The city sits between St. Augustine and Daytona Beach, giving residents access to larger destinations while offering a slower pace at home, with a median monthly rent of $1,466 and a median household income of $74,864. 2. Spring Hill Spring Hill offers Florida retirees a quieter suburban lifestyle, with parks, golf courses, and other activities nearby. Its location also provides access to beaches, Weeki Wachee Springs State Park, and other outdoor recreation while keeping average commute times at 23 minutes and residents within driving distance of the Tampa Bay area. The median household income is $71,158, while the median home value in this small coastal city is $302,212. 1. Homosassa Springs Homosassa Springs took the top spot on US News' ranking of the best places in Florida to retire. The community offers retirees a laid-back lifestyle along Florida's Nature Coast, with easy access to rivers, wildlife, and outdoor activities. The average commute time is 19 minutes, and with a median monthly rent of $864, it's easy to see why some might choose this town to spend their golden years.

item.title: 3 ways people make their kitchens look cheap, according to interior designers
item.description:
Source: Business Insider Score: 5.09
It's a common saying in real estate that kitchens and bathrooms sell homes. It can be easy to miss the mark when trying to create a luxury kitchen, though. That's why Business Insider spoke with two interior designers about the details that can make the space look cheap. Here's what they had to say. Dull colors and lighting It's common for modern kitchens to have neutral color palettes, but the experts said that's often a mistake. Charlotte Eustace, a UK-based interior designer who founded Eustace Studio, said she especially dislikes millennial gray kitchens. "It just looks so cheap," she said, adding that gray can look "cold" in a kitchen. Harsh lighting does the same thing. "If your lighting is very cold or if you're doing all neutral but everything has a cold undertone, I think that can really cheapen it," she said. "Generally, the spaces that feel the most luxurious and welcoming are warmer spaces." Juliana Ghani, an interior designer from Minneapolis, said she tries to avoid "anything that looks sterile" in kitchens, which is often white, black, or gray. In the same vein, she said LED light bulbs are a huge no-no for her. "It looks like an operating room when you have those blue LED lights on your island," she said, adding that warm lighting is "the easiest way to make your kitchen look richer and homey." Pops of color in your cabinetry or wood accents can also help make a kitchen feel warmer. The design is in the details Ghani said basic kitchens often make appliances the focal point of the room, whereas in luxury spaces, they're more hidden. "I think a mistake people make when designing a kitchen, especially an open-concept kitchen, is that they let the appliances dominate the space," Ghani said. "In a luxury kitchen, we would have paneled appliances, integrated hardware, or even different finishes on the actual appliances that kind of hide them in a way." "A row of stainless steel appliances, pretty much, is not giving luxury," she said. Eustace said the smaller details can also make a big difference to how your eye perceives a kitchen as a whole. That includes elements such as cabinet handles, countertop materials, and even outlet panels. "A kitchen can be really nice, and then if I see cup handles or something, immediately I'm just like, 'Oh gosh, that really just cheapens the whole feel of it,'" Eustace said, referring to curved handles that don't look high-end. Upgrading your hardware is an easy way to give your kitchen a luxurious feel, though. Ghani recommends brushed chrome, brushed nickel, or lacquered brass. Too much on the counters Ghani said it's also a mistake to have too much sitting out on your counters because it can look "messy" or "cluttered." At the same time, cookbooks or appliances you use daily on your countertops can help a space look lived in. Eustace agreed, saying you don't want your kitchen to look uninviting. "I think there's an obsession these days with having everything hidden, as if it's like a showroom the whole time and no one lives there," Eustace said. "I don't think people should be afraid to have things out or, you know, have a little bit of mess or clutter." "Things that you're actually using every day, and just signs of life, don't make it look cheap," she added, though she said microwaves sitting on a counter aren't aesthetically pleasing, in her opinion. "It has to make sense for you," Ghani said about what sits on your countertops. "It would be obnoxious if you eat toast every day and you have to take out your toaster." "If you're doing a custom kitchen or you're remodeling, a lot of times we try to fit in a butler's pantry or a walk-in pantry where you can put in a lot of those countertop appliances, your sugar, and your salt and pepper," Ghani added. Most importantly, both designers advised people not to be afraid to bring their own personality to their spaces, as a homey kitchen is the best kitchen.

item.title: DoorDash is set to become a Nevada-incorporated company.
item.description:
Source: Business Insider Score: 4.79
DoorDash is set to become a Nevada-incorporated company. Shareholders controlling 54.2% of the delivery service's voting power agreed to end its incorporation in Delaware and head west, according to a Tuesday filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission. The move was made with the written consent of the shareholders, including cofounders Tony Xu, Andy Fang, and Stanley Tang, according to the filing. DoorDash's board had unanimously recommended reincorporating in Nevada. DoorDash is the latest company to decide to move out of Delaware. While it's long been the top state for companies looking to incorporate, big names from Roblox to VC firm Andreessen Horowitz have left over the last two years. Elon Musk famously reincorporated SpaceX in Texas after a judge in Delaware voided his $55 billion pay package in 2024. DoorDash cited its own concerns about Delaware's legal system in Tuesday's filing. "DoorDash's management and Board believe that the Company will be best positioned to pursue its corporate strategy within the more predictable, statute-based legal environment that Nevada provides," the company wrote. Delaware has a reputation of legal precedents that are favorable to businesses, DoorDash's filing reads. "However, in recent years, a discussion has emerged in the market over the legal landscape in Delaware, including as a result of cases that reached what many viewed as surprising results, an increasingly litigious environment and high-profile litigation outcomes that involved companies with controlling stockholders," it continues. Other states, such as Nevada, "attracted attention as potentially offering a more business-friendly, agile and predictable environment," the company wrote. Do you have a story idea about DoorDash? Contact this reporter at abitter@businessinsider.com or via encrypted messaging app Signal at 808-854-4501. Use a personal email address, a nonwork WiFi network, and a nonwork device; here's our guide to sharing information securely.

item.title: Tesla built a Starlink internet dish into its Cybercab robotaxi
item.description:
Source: Business Insider Score: 4.78
Tesla is giving its Cybercab a little help from another Elon Musk company. On Monday, the EV maker shared photos on X of what it called the "First Cybercab with Starlink integration." The images show a square-like cutout in the roofline, where the satellite internet equipment is built directly into the vehicle. In a subsequent X post, Musk said riders inside the autonomous two-seat car can "watch live sports in 4k or movies or games or productivity." The integration is another example of how Musk's companies are increasingly intertwined. Tesla is using SpaceX's AI personality, Grok, as a voice assistant in its vehicles; SpaceX is buying hundreds of millions of dollars' worth of Tesla Megapacks and cars; and the companies have partnered on a joint chip factory project called Terafab. Those collaborations have inspired rumors of a potential mega-merger between the two companies. Monday's Cybercab post also shows how Tesla plans to keep its future fleet of driverless cars connected. During the automaker's second-quarter earnings call, Musk said that Starlink would help address gaps in cellular coverage as the company expands its self-driving robotaxi service. "We can't have robotaxis getting stuck in these Bermuda Triangles of lack of cellular connectivity," Musk said. "Starlink, with its ability to do connectivity anywhere, is actually quite important, so we don't have robotaxis missing in action."

item.title: TikTok is for the creator middle class, but top earners favor Instagram
item.description:
Source: Business Insider Score: 4.73
TikTok was Julia Kong's biggest source of brand deals when she started her creator career in 2020. Today, Instagram has replaced it as her top revenue driver, though her TikTok following is still vastly larger. "It's what brands would prefer to reference when deciding whether or not to work with you," Kong, who posts about beauty and cinema, said of Instagram. "TikTok is still a great search engine, but I don't think it's as organized or clean-cut as Instagram." Travis Percy, a creator who posts about leadership, said he's also found Instagram to have more potential than TikTok as he has grown. New survey data from the influencer-marketing platform CreatorIQ backs up the sentiment that, as creators grow their careers, Instagram becomes a more lucrative platform than TikTok. In a sample of about 5,000 creators, TikTok ranked first (at 52%) as the leading platform for posting branded content, compared with Instagram at 43%. That flipped with creators earning more than $250,000 a year: 60% named Instagram as their main platform for branded content versus 30% for TikTok. In short: TikTok is for the creator middle class, while top earners favor Instagram. When asked which platform has the best potential to build a business over the long haul, respondents overall valued Instagram (38%) ahead of TikTok (35%) and YouTube (23%). (Among the creators who regularly publish on YouTube, though, more than half considered it their most lucrative platform.) The survey was conducted from May to June, primarily among US creators, and contained influencers from a range of genres and follower counts. Tim Sovay, chief partnerships officer at CreatorIQ, said Instagram is "where brands are spending the most amount of dollars in the category, both in general paid media, but also with creators." "So the nano-micro story starts on TikTok, and then you see people migrate into longer-term and bigger channels and bigger monetization on platforms like Instagram," he continued. What's behind the divide Influencer talent and marketing agencies said they have seen similar dynamics among their clients. Kyle Hjelmeseth, CEO of talent firm G&B Digital Management, said Gen Z creators made TikTok popular in recent years as a place to get your start as a creator. "It's great for virality, it's great for finding an audience, but it was always mired by negative press, so it wasn't seen as a place where I can't throw all my eggs in this basket," he said. "Instagram is the platform that's been consistent and hasn't had any issues." Hjelmeseth said he sees the tide turning, though, with brands showing strong interest in both platforms. TikTok "micro" influencers saw a spike in their average brand partnership rates in the first quarter compared with the year-ago period, according to data from Upfluence, an influencer marketing platform. TikTok also shared internal data showing its creators' business results have accelerated in the past year. The number of creators making branded content deals through its platform grew 90% year over year through May, while creators with 50,000 followers and up saw their monthly earnings rise 40% year over year. Becca Bahrke, CEO of talent firm Illuminate Social, said so far this year, 64% of brand partnerships coming through her firm involved Instagram versus 14% for TikTok. She added that Instagram posts reached their potential audiences faster than TikTok posts, giving brands results to evaluate sooner. Paid boosting helps TikTok Sovay cited a TikTok program called "Spark Ads" as another reason the platform works well for less-established creators. This program lets a brand pay to boost posts, which makes it easy to place a lot of small bets on micro influencers. The advent of TikTok Shop has also benefited small-scale creators who have proliferated in recent years. TikTok positions Shop as a place where creators with as few as 1,000 followers can earn affiliate revenue. EMARKETER, a sibling company of Business Insider, forecast that paid boosting will grow and roughly match what brands pay influencers to post about their products on social media in the US in 2027. "Immediately boosting that content to hit your target audience with Spark Ads has been core to TikTok's strategy," Sovay said. "It's not to say that small creators don't work on Instagram or big creators don't work on TikTok." Lily Comba, CEO and cofounder of the marketing agency Superbloom, said, though, that Spark Ads rates have become increasingly competitive. For that and other reasons, she said Instagram is better for discovery, relationship building, and conversion potential. While YouTube ranked third in the CreatorIQ survey, it drives some of the longest-lasting value from creator content. "The content has a much longer shelf life, audiences tend to be more intentional and engaged, and we're increasingly prioritizing YouTube for our clients as we plan into 2027," she said.

item.title: This Week's Perseid Meteor Shower Could Be the Best Stargazing Event in Years
item.description:
Source: Condé Nast Traveler Score: 6.51
There are few sights that are as awe-inspiring as a sky suddenly alive with shooting stars. During the annual Perseid meteor shower, which occurs in August each year, bright streaks of white, amber, and the occasional emerald flash between familiar constellations, briefly illuminating the darkness before dissolving back into a sky so crowded with stars it hardly seems real. It's one of nature's most mesmerizing performances—and all you have to do is look up. Under ideal dark sky conditions, observers can expect to see anywhere from 50 to 100 meteors an hour during the peak, with activity building after midnight and continuing until dawn. These so-called shooting stars are actually tiny fragments of ancient comet dust—many no larger than grains of sand—slamming into Earth's atmosphere at roughly 37 miles per second. The result?
