But it's not all good news, as the program significantly devalued its award options in major Japanese cities in mid-2026. Even so, it's still possible to get good value from the Choice Privileges program. Let's dive in. Choice Privileges elite status You can qualify for Choice Privileges elite status and milestone rewards through qualifying nights or qualifying credits. Qualifying nights are generally your points-eligible nights, reward nights (including points and cash rates) and nights booked under employee or friends and family rate plans. Meanwhile, qualifying credits consist primarily of base points earned from stays and points earned through qualifying spending on a linked U.S.-issued Choice Privileges credit card. However, Choice treats extended stay properties differently. Stays at WoodSpring Suites don't earn qualifying nights or qualifying credits, while qualifying stays at Everhome Suites, MainStay Suites and Suburban Studios earn qualifying nights and qualifying credits as follows: - Stays of six nights or less: one qualifying night per night completed and 10 qualifying credits per dollar spent - Stays of seven nights or more: one qualifying night per two nights completed (capped at 15 qualifying nights per stay) and five qualifying credits per dollar spent on the first 30 nights of a stay (no qualifying credits for nights 31 and onward) Once you qualify for a specific Choice Privileges tier higher than Member, you'll keep that status through the end of the next calendar year. You must requalify for your status each calendar year to keep it. However, if you don't requalify, Choice Privileges has a soft-landing policy. With this policy, you'll automatically get the status one tier lower than the previous year if you don't requalify for your status. This applies even if you soft-land into your current status, meaning you'll slowly move down the Choice elite status tiers until you reach the Member tier if you fail to requalify for several years in a row. Now, let's look at the Choice Privileges tiers, as well as the milestone rewards you can earn along the way. Choice Privileges Member When you sign up for a Choice Privileges membership, you'll automatically get Member status and the following benefits: - 10 base points per dollar spent at most Choice Hotels properties - 1,000 bonus points after your second qualifying stay and another 1,000 bonus points after your third qualifying stay each calendar year Choice Privileges Gold You'll earn Gold status after completing five qualifying nights or earning 10,000 qualifying credits in a calendar year. However, one easy way to snag Gold status is to have the no-annual-fee Choice Privileges® Mastercard®, which gives cardholders 10 elite qualifying nights each calendar year. Gold members enjoy the following perks on top of those offered to all members: - 10% bonus points on all qualifying stays - A welcome gift (bonus points, a beverage or a snack) at participating hotels - Early check-in and late checkout (only where available) - Room upgrades at Cambria and Ascend Collection brands worldwide and at Radisson, Radisson Blu, Radisson RED, Radisson Collection, Radisson Individuals and Park Plaza brands in North America, Canada, Latin America and the Caribbean (determined by each hotel at check-in and subject to availability; hotels are not required to upgrade rooms to any specific type) - Elite reserved parking (when available) at participating hotels in the U.S. and Canada - Access to an elite customer hotline - A status match to Penn Play Advantage at more than 20 casino hotels nationwide Additionally, points don't expire as long as you remain an elite member. Choice Privileges also lets active-duty military members, veterans and military spouses enjoy Gold status upon request. Choice Gold status is a sweet spot that offers a decent number of benefits, even though the annual qualification requirements are easily obtainable by most travelers. The information for the Choice Privileges Mastercard has been collected independently by The Points Guy. The card details on this page have not been reviewed or provided by the card issuer. Choice Privileges Platinum You'll reach Platinum status after 15 qualifying nights or 30,000 elite qualifying credits in a calendar year. One easy way to maintain Platinum status is to have the Choice Privileges® Select Mastercard® ($95 annual fee), which gives cardholders 20 elite qualifying nights each calendar year. Choice Privileges Platinum benefits include all the perks of Gold status, plus 25% bonus points on all qualifying stays. Since the primary difference between Gold and Platinum status is earning a 25% bonus on qualifying stays instead of 10%, it's not worth chasing for most travelers. However, if you earn Platinum status, the additional bonus points will provide some incremental value. The information for the Choice Privileges Select Mastercard has been collected independently by The Points Guy. The card details on this page have not been reviewed or provided by the card issuer. Choice Privileges Diamond You'll earn Diamond status after 35 qualifying nights or 70,000 qualifying credits in a calendar year. Of course, if you have the Choice Privileges Mastercard or the Choice Privileges Select Mastercard, you'll get elite qualifying nights each calendar year as a cardholder perk. That means you won't need to stay as many nights to secure Diamond status. In addition to the above Platinum benefits, Diamond members get the following perks: - 50% bonus points on all qualifying stays - Complimentary breakfast for you and one registered guest at participating hotel restaurants during stays at Radisson, Radisson Red, Radisson Blu, Radisson Collection, Radisson Individuals and Park Plaza properties in North America, Latin America and the Caribbean - Guaranteed room availability for eligible paid stays when you call at least 48 hours before your stay at participating Ascend Collection and Cambria hotels worldwide and at Radisson, Radisson Red, Radisson Blu, Radisson Collection, Radisson Individuals and Park Plaza hotels in North America, Latin America and the Caribbean (restrictions and blackout periods apply) - A status match to Penn Play Preferred Complimentary breakfast at select brands is where Choice Privileges Diamond status offers significantly more value than Platinum status. If you frequently stay at these brands or value a status match to Penn Play Preferred status, it could be worth striving for Diamond status. Choice Privileges Titanium Finally, you'll secure top-tier Titanium status with 55 qualifying nights or 110,000 qualifying credits in a calendar year. Titanium members enjoy all the perks of Diamond status. Plus, Titanium members receive one Titanium travel award each calendar year. This award reduces the points required for one eligible reward night reservation by 50% and can cover one room for up to seven consecutive nights at a curated selection of properties. You must book and complete your Titanium travel award stay during the calendar year in which the award is issued. But if you don't currently have Titanium status, you'll earn one Titanium travel award in the year you qualify and another in the following year while you have the status. Related: Comparing the best hotel elite status tiers and how to earn them Milestone rewards Choice Privileges members can earn milestone rewards of points or gift cards as they accrue qualifying nights and qualifying credits each calendar year as follows: | Milestone | Points option | Gift card option | |---|---|---| | 10 qualifying nights or 20,000 qualifying credits | 1,500 | $5 | | 20 qualifying nights or 40,000 qualifying credits | 2,500 | $10 | | 25 qualifying nights or 50,000 qualifying credits | 3,000 | $10 | | 30 qualifying nights or 60,000 qualifying credits | 3,500 | $10 | | 40 qualifying nights or 80,000 qualifying credits | 4,500 | $20 | | 45 qualifying nights or 90,000 qualifying credits | 5,000 | $20 | | 50 qualifying nights or 100,000 qualifying credits | 6,500 | $20 | Note that the qualifying night credits you get each year as a Choice Privileges cardholder are elite qualifying but not milestone qualifying. (Spending on your card earns both elite and milestone qualifying credits, though.) Additionally, the gift card option is only available in the U.S. and Canada. How to earn Choice Privileges points Here's a quick overview of the many ways to earn Choice Privileges points. Hotel stays Members earn 10 base points per dollar spent on their room rate (excluding taxes and incidental charges) at most participating Choice hotels, and elite members earn 10% to 50% bonus points based on their status tier. However, you won't earn points on WoodSpring Suites stays, and you'll only earn 5 points per dollar spent on stays of seven to 30 nights at Everhome Suites, MainStay Suites and Suburban Studios. (You won't earn points for nights 31 and beyond.) Plus, you won't earn points for stays in select destinations (see the program's rules and regulations for details). To earn Choice Privileges points at participating properties, you must book an eligible rate directly with Choice Hotels through one of the following channels: the toll-free express reservation line, the Choice Hotels website or mobile app, or directly with a participating hotel. However, even when booked directly, some stays won't be eligible to earn points. These include stays with room rates below $40 a night, certain hotel-initiated promotions, reward night stays and Points Plus Cash reservations. See the rules and regulations for more details. Credit card spending If you frequently stay at Choice properties, you may want to get a cobranded Choice Privileges credit card. You can earn Choice points with the cobranded cards as follows: - Choice Privileges Mastercard (no annual fee): 5 points per dollar spent on stays at participating Choice Hotels properties; 3 points per dollar spent on purchases at gas stations, grocery stores and home improvement stores, plus phone plan services; and 1 point per dollar spent on other purchases - Choice Privileges Select Mastercard ($95 annual fee): 10 points per dollar spent on stays at participating Choice Hotels properties; 5 points per dollar spent on purchases at gas stations, grocery stores and home improvement stores, plus phone plan services; and 1 point per dollar spent on other purchases Related: Best hotel credit cards Transfer rewards from other programs Several programs with transferable currencies partner with Choice Privileges, allowing you to easily get more Choice points: - American Express Membership Rewards: Transfer at a ratio of 1 Amex point to 1 Choice point - Capital One miles: Transfer at a ratio of 1 Capital One mile to 1 Choice point - Citi ThankYou Rewards: Transfer at a ratio of 1 Citi point to 1.5 or 1.05 Choice points, depending on your specific Citi ThankYou Rewards card - Wells Fargo Rewards: Transfer at a ratio of 1 Wells Fargo point to 2 Choice points Buy Choice points Buying Choice points is another way to boost your balance. The cost per point varies depending on how many points you purchase, but you'll typically pay between 1.03 and 1.28 cents per point — not a great deal compared to our August 2026 valuation of 0.7 cents per Choice point. However, you can sometimes pay much less if Choice is offering a discount or bonus promotion. Earn with partners Choice Privileges partners with various programs to let members earn additional points on other activities. These include: - Avis and Budget car rentals: Get up to 35% off and earn Choice points when you rent with Avis or Budget. - Choice Privileges Cruises: Earn Choice points when you book a qualifying cruise through Choice's cruise platform. - E-Rewards: Earn Choice points by taking surveys. Earn when planning events You can earn Choice Privileges points when you host events at eligible Choice hotels. When you associate your Choice Privileges member number with your group's reservation, you'll earn 3 points per dollar spent (up to 150,000 points or more per meeting at Cambria Hotels and unlimited points at Radisson Hotels) on eligible charges, including meeting space, sleeping rooms and food-and-beverage charges. How to redeem Choice Privileges points Now that you know how to earn Choice Privileges points, let's consider the different ways you can redeem Choice points. You'll usually get the most value when you use Choice points for hotel stays, but there are other options. Redeem for free nights Choice Privileges has no set award chart and doesn't sort properties into categories. Although Choice no longer caps award nights at 35,000 points, most award nights still cost between 8,000 and 35,000 points. You can book reward nights up to 50 weeks in advance. You'll occasionally see RewardSaver discounts when you search for reward night stays. Some properties make premium room types or views available with points. In some cases, you may find an upgraded room for the same number of points as a standard room. You can book Points Plus Cash rates at some Choice Hotels if you see the option when you search for a reward night. You won't earn points on the cash portion, as you're effectively buying points with the cash copay. As such, ensure you're buying points at a low enough rate to make doing so worthwhile. You can buy up to 250,000 points per calendar year through these bookings. You can also redeem Choice points for stays at participating Preferred Hotels & Resorts, Westgate Resorts, Bluegreen Vacations properties and Penn Entertainment Hotels. Redeem for special experiences Choice Privileges Experiences lets you bid on exclusive college sports experiences and NASCAR experiences with Choice points. The tickets up for auction change frequently, but you can see what's currently available on the Choice Experiences website. Related: 8 of the most exclusive travel experiences you can book with points and miles Redeem for gift cards You can redeem Choice Privileges points for physical or electronic gift cards to a limited number of retailers such as Amazon, Home Depot, Target, Walmart and Applebee's. In most cases, you can redeem 8,000 points for a $25 gift card, 16,000 points for a $50 gift card or 32,000 points for a $100 gift card. This yields only 0.31 cents per point, so it's best to use other redemption options that provide more value. Donate your points You also have the option to donate your Choice Privileges points to a handful of charities, including the American Red Cross, Boys & Girls Clubs of America and the National Park Foundation. Most of these allow you to donate $5 per 1,000 Choice points redeemed, but you can donate $10 to Polaris per 1,000 Choice points redeemed. This gives you a solid redemption value of 0.5 to 1 cent per point. Related: How you can donate your points and miles to charity Exchange your points for miles If you'd rather have airline miles than hotel points, you can transfer your Choice points to the following loyalty programs online: - Aer Lingus AerClub: Starting at 5,000 points for 1,000 Avios - Aeromexico Rewards: Starting at 5,000 points for 1,000 Aeromexico points - Air Canada Aeroplan: Starting at 5,000 points for 1,000 Aeroplan points - Air France-KLM Flying Blue: Starting at 5,000 points for 1,000 Flying Blue miles - Alaska Airlines Atmos Rewards: Starting at 5,000 points for 1,000 Atmos Rewards points - Avianca Lifemiles: Starting at 5,000 points for 1,000 Lifemiles - British Airways Club: Starting at 5,000 points for 1,000 Avios - Iberia Club: Starting at 5,000 points for 1,000 Avios - LATAM Pass: Starting at 5,000 points for 1,000 LATAM miles - Qantas Frequent Flyer: Starting at 2,000 points for 800 Qantas points - Saudia AlFursan: Starting at 5,000 points for 1,000 AlFursan miles - Southwest Rapid Rewards: Starting at 6,000 points for 1,800 Southwest points - Turkish Airlines Miles&Smiles: Starting at 5,000 points for 1,000 Turkish miles - United MileagePlus: Starting at 5,000 points for 1,000 United miles - Velocity Frequent Flyer: Starting at 2,000 points for 800 Velocity points You'll usually be better off keeping your Choice points and redeeming them for hotel stays, but this option could make sense if you don't frequently stay at Choice Hotels properties and are short a few miles for your next airline redemption. Redeem for cruise credit Finally, you can redeem Choice Privileges points toward a sailing through Choice Privileges Cruises. You'll have to call, but you can redeem 85,000 points for a $250 credit toward your cruise or 160,000 points for a $500 credit. This provides a redemption value of 0.29 or 0.31 cents per point, so it's not a high-value way to redeem Choice points. Maximizing Choice Privileges points As you can see from the above options, redeeming Choice points for award nights is usually the best way to maximize their value. Here are a few tips to get even more value from the Choice Privileges program. Choice Privileges promotions The Choice Privileges program frequently offers promotions to help you save money or earn bonus points. One of the best promotions Choice offers several times each year lets you earn 8,000 Choice points for every two hotel stays. So, it's worth keeping an eye out for promotions if you have stays at Choice Hotels coming up. Sweet spot redemptions There are plenty of opportunities to get outsize value from Choice Privileges points. For example, in Japan, you can book some properties for as few as 8,000 points per night. You can also find centrally located hotels in Europe that can be booked for as little as 8,000 points per night. Choice points can also provide good value in the U.S. For instance, here are some properties near Myrtle Beach, South Carolina, where you can book a weekend night for 15,000 points. Lowest Price Guarantee Choice's Lowest Price Guarantee applies when you book directly with Choice and then find a lower publicly available price within 24 hours of booking. You must book at least 48 hours before a 6 a.m. arrival on the first day of your booking and complete the claim form within 24 hours of booking. Within 48 hours of your claim, a Choice Hotels representative will contact you. If your claim is approved, Choice will not only honor the lower rate for your stay but also give you a $50 reward card if you're a U.S. or Canadian resident. If you're an international resident, the first night of your stay will be free. Match up to Choice Privileges Platinum status If you have elite status with another hotel loyalty program and live in the U.S., Canada, Europe, the Caribbean, Latin America or Mexico, you can take advantage of Choice's status match program for tiers up to Choice Platinum. To use this status match, U.S. and Canadian members must send their name, Choice Privileges member number and a screenshot of their current account statement with another hotel loyalty program to Status_Match@choicehotels.com. European members can send this information to Status_Match_EU@choicehotels.com, while Caribbean, Latin American and Mexican members should send their information to CALA.statusmatch@choicehotels.com. Based on the information you provided, Choice Privileges may match you up to Platinum status. If you match between January and June, you'll keep the matched status through the end of the year. But if you match between July and December, you'll keep the status through the end of the following year. As such, July is generally the best time to request the match because a successful match should last through the end of the following calendar year. Bottom line Choice Privileges may not offer the rich, consistent elite benefits of some competing hotel loyalty programs, but it can still deliver significant value. Reward nights start at just 6,000 points, Choice has a large footprint across multiple price points and its U.S. credit cards can accelerate both elite status and milestone rewards. The program is especially compelling when you find RewardSaver nights, discover a premium room bookable for the same number of points as a standard room or book a high-value reward night. However, award costs can change without notice, and elite benefits vary considerably by brand and property. As a result, the best way to use Choice Privileges is usually to focus less on earning status and more on redeeming points in high-value ways. Frequently asked questions Choice Privileges is free to join. Once you join, you can earn points on eligible Choice hotel stays and access member rates, promotions and other perks. Choice Privileges points generally expire after 18 months of account inactivity. However, points do not expire while you have Choice Privileges elite status. Eligible award stays booked with Choice points, including Points Plus Cash stays, generally earn elite qualifying nights and milestone qualifying nights. However, you won't earn points, elite qualifying credits or milestone qualifying credits on reward nights and Points Plus Cash stays. The annual elite qualifying nights awarded by U.S.-issued Choice Privileges credit cards count toward elite status but not toward milestone rewards. However, you'll earn elite qualifying credits and milestone qualifying credits when you make eligible purchases with these cards. Choice reward nights start at 6,000 points, although most awards cost 8,000 points or more. Choice does not publish a fixed award chart, so rates vary by hotel and date.

item.title: Chase Points Boost: How to get more value from your points in Chase Travel
item.description:
Source: The Points Guy Score: 5.55
Chase Points Boost: How to get more value from your points in Chase Travel In 2025, Chase introduced Points Boost as a way to get outsized value from your Chase Ultimate Rewards points without having to transfer them to hotel and airline partners. Available on eligible Chase cards, including the Chase Sapphire Preferred® Card (see rates and fees), the Chase Sapphire Reserve® (see rates and fees) and the Chase Sapphire Reserve for Business℠ (see rates and fees), Points Boost lets you redeem Chase Ultimate Rewards points for select hotels and flights booked through Chase Travel℠ at higher values than the standard 1 cent per point. Depending on the booking, your points can be worth up to 1.5–2 cents each, and occasionally go even higher. That's surprisingly close to TPG's August 2026 valuation of Chase Ultimate Rewards points at 2.05 cents apiece, without having to learn airline or hotel transfer partners. Here's how Chase Points Boost works — and how to decide when it's your best redemption option. What is Chase Points Boost? Points Boost is a feature that lets you book select hotels and flights through Chase Travel for fewer points than you'd pay at the standard 1 cent-per-point redemption rate. For cardholders with the Chase Sapphire Reserve or Sapphire Reserve for Business, Points Boost values can typically reach up to 2 cents per point. For eligible cards such as the Chase Sapphire Preferred, Points Boost values typically top out around 1.5 cents per point, though these values can vary. One thing we've noticed is that the $95 Sapphire Preferred will occasionally receive a better Points Boost redemption than the Sapphire Reserve, so don't automatically assume the more expensive card always offers the best value. | Card | Hotels Points Boost | Airfare Points Boost | |---|---|---| | | Select hotels, including The Edit by Chase Travel: Up to 2 cents per point | Flights with select airlines: Up to 2 cents per point | | | Select hotels: Up to 1.5 cents per point (not eligible for bookings through The Edit) | Flights with select airlines: Up to 1.75 cents per point | You'll often find Points Boost available at Chase's curated list of The Edit properties, available for booking by Sapphire Reserve and Sapphire Reserve for Business cardholders, but it also appears at many more budget-friendly hotels. Related: What's the difference between Chase's The Edit properties and Points Boost? How to use Chase Points Boost To use Points Boost, simply search for flights or hotels in Chase Travel the same way you normally would. If you want to prioritize Points Boost-eligible options, select the "Points Boost only" filter shown below. This narrows your results to hotels and flights offering boosted redemption values for your travel dates. You can also identify eligible bookings by the small rocket icon that appears next to the points price. You may also notice the 1.65 cents-per-point valuation highlighted in blue. That's not part of Chase Travel itself; it's displayed through a third-party tool called Points Path. There are free membership levels available with Points Path, and having that additional data displayed makes it much easier to spot some of the best redemption opportunities at a glance. Tips for using Points Boost for hotels Points Boost is most reliably available for Chase's The Edit Hotels, a program available to those with the Chase Sapphire Reserve or Sapphire Reserve for Business. These stays come with an included breakfast for two, a $100 property credit and a few other perks and amenities. Points Boost becomes especially valuable when you can stack it with one of the Sapphire Reserve's two annual up-to-$250 The Edit statement credits. A minimum two-night stay is required. Here's one example. This two-night stay at the Westin Anaheim Resort, just steps from Disneyland, costs $865 or 52,420 Chase points with Points Boost at 1.65 cents per point. Now apply one of the up to $250 The Edit credits. Your out-of-pocket cost drops to $615. If you then use Points Boost at checkout to cover the rest, you'd redeem just 37,269 points (at 1.65 cents each) plus the $250 charged to your Sapphire Reserve to trigger the statement credit. Related: How to stack using Points Boost and Chase's $250 The Edit credit That's effectively 18,636 Chase points per night. Booking those same two nights directly through Marriott Bonvoy would require 108,000 Marriott points. The same strategy works with the Sapphire Preferred's annual $100 Chase Travel hotel statement credit. Tips for using Points Boost for airfare While I reliably find Points Boost hotel options, flight availability is somewhat less consistent. It's uncommon to see Points Boost on everyday domestic economy itineraries, but I've found some better values on long-haul premium cabin flights, where Points Boost can occasionally beat transferring points to an airline — particularly when airline award availability through transfer partners is limited. Even so, I always compare: - Points Boost redemption price - Transfer partner award price - Cash fare I'd recommend using Seats.aero to start that comparison shopping. An added perk of booking via Chase Travel is that the airline typically treats the flight as a paid fare, so it may help you earn airline miles and frequent flyer status. Is Points Boost worth it? Whether Points Boost is the best redemption depends on three things: - The Points Boost redemption value - How many points a transfer partner would require - Whether Chase Travel's cash price is competitive If you were already planning to redeem Chase points through Chase Travel, getting more than 1 cent per point with Points Boost is almost always a better outcome. But generally speaking, the higher the return per point via Points Boost — especially as it approaches the 2-cent-per-point mark — the better of a deal it generally is, though finding awards at that high water mark has gotten harder over the months. That said, if the redemption is closer to 1.5 cents per point, it's still worth comparing transfer partner pricing before booking. TPG Tip: Chase Travel has started to allow some customers to price-match hotels to non-Chase Travel prices, which could be a great way to use your Chase points and lock in the best price you can find. Related: Who are the Chase Ultimate Rewards airline and hotel transfer partners? Bottom line Chase has made several changes to how points are redeemed in Chase Travel over the past year, but Points Boost remains a positive addition. While 2-cent-per-point redemptions aren't as common as they were at launch, it's still possible to find excellent values — particularly on hotels and some premium-cabin flights, especially when stacking with some of Chase's hotel statement credits. As a rule, I always compare Points Boost against transfer partner pricing before redeeming. If the redemption is approaching 2 cents per point, it's often difficult to beat that value unless you've found an exceptional airline or hotel sweet spot. For those who have had their Chase cards for a while and were grandfathered into the 'old' redemption rates of 1.25 cents or 1.5 cents, depending on the Chase card, you may still have points available to use at those fixed redemption rates until Oct. 26, 2027. For everyone else, Points Boost is one of the easiest ways to stretch Chase Ultimate Rewards without needing to learn the ins and outs of airline and hotel transfer partners. Related reading: TPG featured card | 4X | Earn 4X Membership Rewards® points per dollar spent on purchases at restaurants worldwide, on up to $50,000 in purchases per calendar year, then 1X points for the rest of the year. | | 4X | Earn 4X Membership Rewards® points per dollar spent at US supermarkets, on up to $25,000 in purchases per calendar year, then 1X points for the rest of the year. | | 5X | New! Earn 5X Membership Rewards® points on prepaid hotel stays booked through AmexTravel.com or the Amex Travel App. | | 3X | Earn 3X Membership Rewards® points on flights booked through AmexTravel.com, the Amex Travel App, or purchased directly from airlines. | | 2X | Earn 2X Membership Rewards® points on prepaid car rentals booked through AmexTravel.com or the Amex Travel App and cruises booked and paid through AmexTravel.com. | | 1X | Earn 1X Membership Rewards® point per dollar spent on all other eligible purchases. |

item.title: How to save at least $1 per gallon on gas every week this summer with OnePay
item.description:
Source: The Points Guy Score: 5.42
How to save at least $1 per gallon on gas every week this summer with OnePay OnePay, a consumer financial technology company with ties to Walmart, is giving users at least $1 per gallon back on gas purchased on Wednesdays through Sept. 15, ideal for those filling up before, during and after those long summer vacation road trips. AAA put the national average for a gallon of regular gas at just over $4 on Aug. 5, so with this $1 back per gallon offer, you could get roughly a quarter off the average pump price before factoring in additional savings through a fuel rewards program or one of the best gas credit cards. To take advantage of this deal, here's everything you need to know. Related: Get up to 5% cash back on Walmart purchases with the new OnePay CashRewards Card How the OnePay Wednesday deal works OnePay runs rotating gas offers inside its app (one of which you must activate before you fill up), and each one carries its own cash-back rate. The Wednesday promotion adds $1 per gallon on top of whatever that offer already pays and any cash back you earn from selecting gas as your monthly cash-back category, so you have the potential to save more than $1 per gallon. Rewards are posted as OnePay Points that you can redeem as a deposit into a OnePay account and use for future gas purchases or anything else you pay by card. The bonus only applies to purchases made on a Wednesday, which OnePay defines as midnight to 11:59 p.m. PDT. Drivers on the East Coast should pay close attention to the time when planning their fill-ups, as the qualifying window spans a couple of days for them (opening at 3 a.m. EDT on Wednesdays and closing at 2:59 a.m. on Thursdays). Because the promotion ends Sept. 15, which falls on a Tuesday, only five qualifying Wednesday dates remain for this promotion: Aug. 12, Aug. 19, Aug. 26, Sept. 2 and Sept. 9. Related: 7 tips to get the most out of a tank of gas What you need to do to save at least $1 per gallon on gas this summer To save on gas through this OnePay deal, you'll need to take the following steps: - Download and open the OnePay app, and go to the Rewards section. - Activate a gas offer at a participating station near you. - Fill up on one of the remaining qualifying Wednesday dates. - Pay with an eligible OnePay payment method. If you are paying with the OnePay CashRewards Card (see rates and fees) or a third-party card linked to your OnePay Wallet, OnePay requires you to tap or swipe the physical card (not a virtual one), so don't forget this before you leave the house. OnePay debit cards and OnePay builder cards can earn either way. Three key restrictions apply: - Gas offers are not available in New Jersey or Wisconsin. - Cash-back caps vary by offer. OnePay's terms tie the $1 off to the limits of whichever gas offer you activate, and those limits can be spending caps or gallon caps that differ from one station to the next. Check the individual offer in the app before you start pumping to ensure you will get at least $1 back per gallon on a full tank of gas. - OnePay reserves the right to modify or cancel the bonus at any time, with or without notice. Related: How to use GasBuddy to beat rising fuel prices Bottom line A dollar per gallon back is a generous return on a purchase you were making anyway, and the fact that it stacks with OnePay's standard gas offers makes it even better. If you live near a participating station (there are over 18,000 nationwide), it's worth checking the app before your next fill-up. Take the time now to download the app and activate the offer. Then, try and time your regular fill-ups to fall on Wednesdays between now and Sept. 9 for maximum savings. Related reading:

item.title: Avios launches handy new tool to help you find British Airways, Iberia and Aer Lingus award seats faster
item.description:
Source: The Points Guy Score: 5.41
Avios launches handy new tool to help you find British Airways, Iberia and Aer Lingus award seats faster If you have ever been frustrated trying to redeem your Avios flying on British Airways, Iberia or Aer Lingus because you could only search for availability one day at a time, help has arrived. International Airlines Group (the parent company of these three airlines plus Vueling and Level) has added a calendar-based reward flight search to the Avios website that displays an entire month of award availability in a single view, covering flights operated by British Airways, Iberia and Aer Lingus to book via British Airways Club, Iberia Club and Aer Lingus AerClub programs. Best of all, it costs nothing to use. You just need a free Avios loyalty account. Here's how it works and what you need to know to maximize your Avios. How the new Avios calendar search works Say you're looking for two seats to fly from Miami International Airport (MIA) to London in May next year (an ideal month to visit the United Kingdom) on British Airways. Set your departure and arrival airports in the new Find Reward Flights tool, the number of travelers and the month you want to fly, as well as whether you want one-way or round-trip flights. Ignore the reference to having a Companion Voucher. Select U.K. American Express cardholders who hold a Companion Voucher from a cobranded British Airways card receive additional award seats, and while Chase offers a similar Travel Together Ticket on its U.S. Avios credit cards, there are unfortunately no additional seats for these ticket holders beyond what regular Avios members can access. The search results will then let you filter by cabin type (let's say you're aiming for lie-flat business class). A half circle means limited availability, while a full circle means good availability. Hovering over an available date reveals how many seats are on offer, which cabins they are in and the Avios price. You can click the specific date for more details on flight times, seat availability and Avios rate. When you select the seat you want, you can then click through and book it through the Avios program of the operating airline, in this case, the British Airways Club program. You can also use this to find flights operated by Iberia and Aer Lingus, which is especially handy given the great sweet spots Iberia offers on nonstop flights to Spain, combined with low taxes and fees. What the tool cannot do yet There are three limitations to this new tool worth noting: - It shows nonstop flights only, so connecting itineraries are currently invisible, though Avios says that capability is coming. - It also does not display total taxes and carrier-imposed surcharges, which vary enormously between these three airlines, with British Airways-operated flights often attracting large surcharges. - You cannot book on the Avios site; once you find a seat, you are sent to the operating airline's website to complete the redemption, which may be frustrating if you want to, say, book an Aer Lingus flight but only have an Iberia Club account. Because availability is concentrated at each carrier's hub, the tool works best for point-to-point searches from London's Heathrow Airport (LHR), Adolfo Suárez Madrid-Barajas Airport (MAD) and Dublin Airport (DUB). Run separate searches from each if your route could plausibly connect through more than one. Qatar Airways and Finnair, both of which also use Avios, are not included. Related: What it's like flying Aer Lingus' Airbus A321XLR to Ireland How to earn Avios One of the reasons Avios are so valuable is how easy they are to earn. In addition to cobranded cards that earn Avios directly, British Airways Club, Aer Lingus AerClub and Iberia Club are all transfer partners for Chase Ultimate Rewards points, American Express Membership Rewards points, Bilt Points, Wells Fargo Rewards points and Marriott Bonvoy points. Related: The Amex transfer bonus I've waited a year for is back: Get 30% more Avios British Airways is also a transfer partner for Capital One miles, and Qatar Airways Privilege Club (which uses Avios as its loyalty currency) is a transfer partner of Citi ThankYou Rewards points. You can easily transfer your Avios between any of these airline loyalty programs at no cost as many times as you like. The following cards all currently offer substantial welcome bonuses that you can easily convert to Avios: - American Express® Gold Card: Find out your offer and see if you are eligible for as high as 100,000 Membership Rewards points after spending $8,000 on purchases in the first six months of card membership. Welcome offers vary, and you may not be eligible for an offer. - American Express Platinum Card®: Find out your offer and see if you are eligible for as high as 175,000 Membership Rewards points after spending $12,000 on purchases in the first six months of card membership. Welcome offers vary, and you may not be eligible for an offer. - Capital One Venture Rewards Credit Card: Earn 75,000 bonus miles after spending $4,000 on purchases in the first three months from account opening. - Capital One Venture X Rewards Credit Card: Earn 75,000 bonus miles after spending $4,000 on purchases in the first three months from account opening. - Chase Sapphire Preferred® Card (see rates and fees): Earn 75,000 bonus points after spending $5,000 on purchases in the first three months from account opening. - Chase Sapphire Reserve® (see rates and fees): Earn 100,000 bonus points after spending $6,000 on purchases in the first three months from account opening. - Ink Business Preferred® Credit Card (see rates and fees): Earn 100,000 bonus points after spending $8,000 on purchases in the first three months from account opening. Bottom line This new Find Reward Flights tool is a handy way to quickly find nonstop Avios award availability flying British Airways, Iberia and Aer Lingus. There are some functionality issues like the inability to show connecting itineraries and no information on those pesky surcharges. However, hopefully this will be fixed soon. If you are looking to fly nonstop to London, Madrid or Dublin, it should be a real time-saver and is free, unlike most third-party tools that can help you find availability quickly.

item.title: Which of the 4 Wyndham Rewards credit cards is right for you?
item.description:
Source: The Points Guy Score: 5.35
Which of the 4 Wyndham Rewards credit cards is right for you? Wyndham and Barclays refreshed their cobranded credit card portfolio in June, offering travelers four distinct options based on how often they stay with Wyndham and which benefits they value most. The lineup now ranges from a no-annual-fee card for occasional Wyndham guests to a premium personal card designed for travelers who can maximize annual statement credits and elite perks, plus a business card for owners whose spending aligns with its bonus categories. The right card depends on how often you stay with Wyndham, whether you value premium travel perks and which spending categories fit your everyday (or business) expenses. Here's a closer look at each Wyndham Rewards credit card to help you decide which one deserves a spot in your wallet. The information for the Wyndham Rewards Earner, Earner Plus, Earner Premier and Earner Business cards has been collected independently by The Points Guy. The card details on this page have not been reviewed or provided by the card issuer. Wyndham credit cards Here's an overview of each card, its annual fee and who it's best suited for: | Card | Annual fee | Best for | |---|---|---| | Wyndham Rewards Earner® Card | $0 | Occasional Wyndham guests who don't want to pay an annual fee | | Wyndham Rewards Earner® Plus Card | $95 | Travelers who stay with Wyndham several times a year and want the best overall value | | Wyndham Rewards Earner® Premier Card | $395 | Travelers who can maximize statement credits and premium Wyndham benefits | | Wyndham Rewards Earner® Business Card | $149 | Business owners whose expenses align with the card's bonus categories | Earner Best for: Occasional Wyndham guests who don't want to pay an annual fee Welcome bonus: Earn up to 75,000 bonus points: Earn 30,000 bonus points after spending $1,000 on purchases in the first 90 days from account opening, plus 45,000 additional bonus points after spending $500 at Wyndham properties in the first 180 days from account opening. Annual fee: $0 If you stay with Wyndham once or twice a year, the Earner offers a simple, no-annual-fee way to earn points. It earns elevated rewards on Wyndham stays, plus bonus rewards on gas, electric vehicle charging, grocery (excluding Target and Walmart) and dining purchases, making it easy to keep earning between stays. Cardholders also get automatic Gold status, with preferred room selection, late checkout (where available) and a 10% discount on award stays. These are useful perks for occasional guests, but intentionally lighter than those on annual-fee cards. If you stay with Wyndham several times a year, the Earner Plus delivers greater long-term value. To learn more, read our full review of the Earner. Earner Plus Best for: Travelers who stay with Wyndham several times a year and want the best overall value Welcome bonus: Earn up to 100,000 points: Earn 45,000 points after spending $1,000 on purchases in the first 90 days from account opening, plus an additional 55,000 points after spending $500 at Hotels by Wyndham in the first 180 days from account opening. Annual fee: $95 For many Wyndham loyalists, the Earner Plus strikes the best balance between cost and value. Its bonus categories extend beyond Wyndham stays to travel, dining and grocery purchases, so everyday spending earns points too — and for anyone staying with Wyndham several times a year, that easily justifies the $95 fee. Cardholders get 15,000 bonus points each anniversary, Diamond status for the first year (Platinum after), a free-night certificate worth up to 15,000 points (after five or more stays in a calendar year), up to $25 in statement credits every six months on meal delivery purchases, and a 10% discount on award stays. Compared to the no-fee Earner, that's a meaningfully richer benefit set for a modest cost increase, making the Earner Plus the strongest overall value in the lineup for regular Wyndham guests. To learn more, read our full review of the Earner Plus. Earner Premier Best for: Travelers who can maximize annual statement credits and premium Wyndham benefits Welcome bonus: Earn up to 120,000 points: Earn 90,000 points after spending $6,000 on purchases in the first 120 days from account opening, plus an additional 30,000 points after spending $750 at Hotels by Wyndham in the first 180 days from account opening. Annual fee: $395 The Earner Premier pays for itself through consistent use, not just frequent stays. Add up the recurring credits — up to $120 a year for food delivery, $100 for streaming, $65 toward a wholesale club membership and $100 for spending at least $100 at Wyndham hotels — and you're already close to offsetting the $395 fee before factoring in any travel. Automatic Diamond status, 25% off award stays and 30,000 anniversary points then push the value well past breakeven for anyone who stays at Wyndham even a few times a year. The tradeoff: these are use-it-or-lose-it credits. Skip a few months of streaming or food delivery, and the math stops working in your favor — in which case, the Earner Plus is the smarter choice. To learn more, read our full review of the Earner Premier. Earner Business Best for: Business owners whose expenses align with the card's bonus categories Welcome bonus: Earn up to 100,000 points: Earn 45,000 points after spending $3,000 on purchases in the first 90 days from account opening, plus an additional 55,000 points after spending $500 at Hotels by Wyndham in the first 180 days from account opening. Annual fee: $149 Small-business owners who spend on advertising, gas, office supplies, shipping and Wyndham stays should take a close look at the Earner Business. The card earns 8 points per dollar at Hotels by Wyndham and 5 points per dollar on gas, EV charging, marketing, advertising, office supply stores and shipping purchases (plus 1 point per dollar on everything else). Add in automatic Diamond status, 15,000 anniversary points, 20% fewer points needed for free nights and a $65 annual wholesale club credit, and frequent business spenders can rack up points fast. If your spending doesn't align with those categories, one of Wyndham's personal cards is likely a better fit. To learn more, read our full review of the Earner Business. Which Wyndham card is right for you? No single Wyndham card is the best choice for everyone. Instead, the right card depends on how often you stay with Wyndham, whether you value elite status and premium perks, and if you can maximize each card's bonus categories. Choose the: - Earner if you want a no-annual-fee way to earn Wyndham points. - Earner Plus if you stay with Wyndham several times a year and want the best overall value. - Earner Premier if you'll maximize its recurring statement credits and premium Wyndham benefits. - Earner Business if you're a small-business owner whose spending aligns with its bonus categories. Related: The ultimate guide to earning and redeeming with Wyndham Rewards Bottom line Wyndham's four-card lineup means there's no need to settle for a card that's almost right. Match the annual fee to how often you actually stay with Wyndham, be honest about whether you'll use the statement credits and elite perks, and let your spending (personal or business) point you to the right bonus categories. Get that match right, and any of these cards can turn routine spending into free nights. Related: The best hotel credit cards

item.title: I toured the 'Miracle on the Hudson' plane — here’s what surprised me
item.description:
Source: The Points Guy Score: 5.24
I toured the 'Miracle on the Hudson' plane — here’s what surprised me I was worried that the "Miracle on the Hudson Experience" at the Sullenberger Aviation Museum would be a Disney-like ride, akin to flight-theater attractions that simulate flying over a city. To my relief, that's not what the museum experience was about. "Miracle on the Hudson" refers to the Jan. 15, 2009, incident in which US Airways Flight 1549 struck a flock of geese, resulting in engine failure. Captain Chesley "Sully" Sullenberger managed to land the plane safely in New York's Hudson River, and all 155 people aboard (150 passengers, three flight attendants and two pilots) miraculously survived. The entire recovered US Airways Flight 1549 Airbus A320 — including the fuselage, wings and tail — is the centerpiece of the recently revamped and much-expanded museum, which is located near Charlotte Douglas International Airport (CLT). In addition to seeing the plane, visitors can watch a short documentary about the incident, explore a wide variety of related exhibits and join "passenger talks" where survivors of US Airways Flight 1549 share their stories. But the museum knows some visitors want more. "This plane has transitioned from a regular, everyday commercial aircraft to one of the most important and significant aviation artifacts of the 21st century," said Shelby Dains, collections specialist at the museum. So, in early 2026, the museum introduced the Miracle on the Hudson Experience, a small-group, guided, interactive tour that shares additional information about the event and its aftermath and allows visitors to ask questions. "It is not just somebody talking at you for two hours. You have time to discuss all the things that you're interested in with somebody who's an expert on the subject," Dains said. "Everyone also gets a boarding pass that tells a story about a passenger, a first responder or crew member and you follow that person's story throughout the entire experience." My pretend boarding pass was for Vince Lombardi — not the famed football coach, but the captain of the Thomas Jefferson ferry, which was the first boat on the scene. With his crew, Lombardi rescued 56 people from the freezing water. During my tour, I was reminded why the Miracle on the Hudson plane was on display in Charlotte rather than at the Smithsonian National Air and Space Museum in Washington, D.C., or perhaps the Museum of Flight in Seattle. "We were one of the few museums that had the room and could make a commitment to display the entire plane," Dains said. "For example, we can allow visitors to see the damage at the back of the plane and the way that the straps used to pull the aircraft out of the Hudson River damaged the skin of the fuselage, as well as other aspects of the recovery." Another reason the plane ended up in Charlotte is that US Airways Flight 1549, which was departing from New York City's LaGuardia Airport (LGA), was en route to Charlotte, and most of the passengers on board lived or worked there. One of the most interesting aspects of the tour came at the end, when participants were invited to "glove up" so they could handle some of the recovered items from the flight's crew and passengers. The artifacts include personal possessions from the pilot (and museum namesake) who recently shared news of his Alzheimer's diagnosis. How to book the Miracle on the Hudson experience The museum offers these tours on Wednesdays, Fridays and most Saturdays from 10:45 a.m. to 12:45 p.m. Tickets cost $35 (including the $25 general admission fee), and you can purchase them up to two months in advance. Tour groups are limited to 14 people, ages 13 and up, so if you're making a special trip to visit the museum, it's a good idea to book ahead. What else is on display at the Sullenberger Aviation Museum? While the Miracle on the Hudson aircraft is the centerpiece of the Sullenberger Aviation Museum, there's a lot more aviation history to see and experience there. The museum first opened in 1992 as the Carolinas Aviation Museum, displaying a jumble of aircraft and aviation artifacts in one hangar. That historic WPA-era hangar now houses one gallery of the expanded, rebranded and now Smithsonian-affiliated Sullenberger Aviation Museum; it also displays a historic World War II-era Douglas DC-3 airplane and a variety of aircraft and artifacts related to aviation history in North and South Carolina. The 35,000-square-foot main exhibit building houses the Miracle on the Hudson airplane as well as more than 30 other aircraft, hundreds of historical artifacts and educational exhibits about the aviation and aerospace industry. Visitors can also test their flight skills on a variety of aircraft using computer-based flight simulators, design airworthy gliders and other projects in the hands-on, all-ages makerspace and sit in the outdoor bleachers watching planes land and takeoff from CLT and from the Charlotte Air National Guard base next door.

item.title: A guide to Capital One's Spark business cards
item.description:
Source: The Points Guy Score: 5.20
A guide to Capital One's Spark business cards Editor's Note Capital One offers an expansive suite of personal cards, some of which are at the top of our lists, but it also offers a family of cards designed for businesses. These cards are known as the Spark cards, and they earn cash back. You can currently apply for three Spark cards: the Capital One Spark Cash Plus, Capital One Spark Cash and the Capital One Spark Cash Select. With these cards' similar names and earning rates, let's dive into the differences and examine the cards and their welcome offers. Comparison of the Capital One Spark business cards | Card name | Welcome bonus | Key benefits | Annual fee | |---|---|---|---| | | Earn a one-time $2,000 cash bonus, and for a limited time, earn a $500 Capital One Business Travel credit after spending $30,000 on purchases within the first three months of account opening. Plus, earn an additional $2,000 cash bonus for every $500,000 spent during the first year. | | $150 | | | Earn a $1,000 cash bonus, and for a limited time, earn a $250 Capital One Business Travel credit after spending $10,000 on purchases within the first three months of account opening. | | $0 introductory annual fee for the first year, then $95 | | | Earn a $750 cash bonus after spending $6,000 on purchases within the first three months of account opening. | | $0 | Related: Complete guide to saving money with Capital One Offers Capital One Spark Cash Plus If your business spends a lot each month, consider the Spark Cash Plus. Welcome bonus Earn a one-time $2,000 cash bonus, and for a limited time, earn a $500 Capital One Business Travel credit after spending $30,000 on purchases within the first three months of account opening. Plus, earn an additional $2,000 cash bonus for every $500,000 spent during the first year. Annual fee This card charges a $150 annual fee. Rewards - 5% cash back on hotels and rental cars booked through Capital One Business Travel. - An unlimited 2% cash back on all other purchases. Who should apply? The Spark Cash Plus carries a $150 annual fee. Businesses with high spending should consider this card for its lucrative welcome bonus, which offers unlimited bonus-earning potential in the first year. Plus, if you spend $150,000 or more in a calendar year, your annual fee will be refunded. To learn more, read our full review of the Capital One Spark Cash Plus. Learn more: Capital One Spark Cash Plus Capital One Spark Cash If you'd like to earn unlimited cash back for a lower annual fee, the Spark Cash could be a great fit. Welcome bonus Earn a $1,000 cash bonus, and for a limited time, earn a $250 Capital One Business Travel credit after spending $10,000 on purchases within the first three months of account opening. Annual fee You'll have a $0 introductory annual fee for the first year, then pay a $95 annual fee with this card. Rewards - 5% cash back on hotels and rental cars booked through Capital One Business Travel. - An unlimited 2% cash back on all other purchases. Who should apply? Those looking to earn cash back and redeem any amount at any time should consider this card, as it lets you recoup your expenses and invest them right back into your business. While the card doesn't have many standout benefits, it is incredibly simple to use and ensures you'll earn at least 2% cash back on all purchases. However, you may have a hard time justifying the card's $95 annual fee after the first year, unless you're spending enough to recoup the annual fee in cash back. To learn more, read our full review of the Capital One Spark Cash. Learn more: Capital One Spark Cash Capital One Spark Cash Select For a no-annual-fee business card, the Capital One Spark Cash Select is a solid choice. Welcome bonus Earn a $750 cash bonus after spending $6,000 on purchases within the first three months of account opening. Annual fee This card does not charge an annual fee. Rewards - 5% cash back on hotels and rental cars booked through Capital One Business Travel. - An unlimited 1.5% cash back on all other purchases. Who should apply? The Spark Cash Select has simple, easy-to-remember earning rates with no annual fee or foreign transaction fees. Business owners looking to earn at least 1.5% cash back on all purchases should consider this card. To learn more, read our full review of the Capital One Spark Cash Select. Learn more: Capital One Spark Cash Select Which Capital One Spark card is right for you? If you're deciding between the Capital One Spark cards, consider: - Whether you want to pay an annual fee - How many bonus categories you want access to - Welcome bonus spending requirements If you can meet a high spending requirement for a welcome offer and don't mind paying an annual fee, the Capital One Spark Cash Plus could be a great choice. If you're willing to pay a lower annual fee and can spend $10,000 on a new card in three months, consider the Capital One Spark Cash. Finally, if you prefer no annual fee and a lower minimum spending requirement for the welcome offer, you're a solid candidate for the Capital One Spark Cash Select. Related: Business cards vs. personal cards: Key differences Can I have more than one Spark credit card from Capital One? Yes, you can hold more than one Capital One Spark card at the same time. It's important to note that you can only apply for one Capital One card every six months. Considering that, make sure to spread your applications out over a long enough time period. Related: The ultimate guide to credit card application restrictions Bottom line Capital One's Spark business cards can provide an excellent path for business owners to maximize their rewards strategy. It can also be a great way to separate business and personal expenses. If you plan to apply for one or more of these cards, it's generally recommended that you apply for no more than one personal and one business card with Capital One in a 60-day window. If you're denied, you can always call the reconsideration line to try and get your application approved. The Spark business cards can be a great addition to your business as they offer simplicity and flexibility with earning and redeeming rewards. Related: How to apply for a Capital One business credit card

item.title: Washington, DC's Reagan National Airport plans $800 million expansion
item.description:
Source: The Points Guy Score: 5.02
Washington, DC's Reagan National Airport plans $800 million expansion Southwest Airlines flyers have something to look forward to at Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport (DCA) soon. The Metropolitan Washington Airports Authority, which operates DCA, is planning a new nine-gate concourse for Terminal 1, as shown in environmental documents for the project released in July. The facility would replace the midcentury concourse and rotunda — known locally as "the banjo" for its shape like the instrument — that dates to 1970. The concourse could open as soon as 2031, and a new "processor" building for check-in and baggage claim as part of a later phase two, according to MWAA financial documents. The estimated cost of the projects was $835 million in 2025. Southwest Airlines — the main user of Terminal 1 — would likely use the new concourse, as would Air Canada and Frontier Airlines. "We look forward to the ultimate completion of the project," a Southwest spokesperson said, adding that the airline is working with the airport authority on the project. An MWAA spokesperson declined to comment further on the project. The upgrade to DCA comes just five years after the airport completed the $1 billion Project Journey. That expansion included a new 14-gate concourse (the E Gates), which replaced the dreaded Gate 35X; it also included two new security checkpoints, allowing the National Hall main concourse to move inside security. The airport authority is also pursuing a $22.5 billion redevelopment of another Washington, D.C.-area airport, Dulles International Airport (IAD). The IAD redevelopment is championed by the Trump administration and United Airlines. The new DCA concourse project would completely reorganize how travelers use Terminal 1. To clarify, this is the older, original terminal at the airport, including the landmarked 1941 historic terminal, and not Terminal 2, which opened in 1997. Under the plan, travelers would no longer check in and drop their bags in a lobby far from the Metro and Terminal 2. Instead, they would use the new multilevel processor building on the existing taxi staging lot between terminals 1 and 2. They would descend from check-in to the existing south checkpoint in Terminal 2. From there, they would make a U-turn and walk back south through an enlarged corridor past the B gates (currently used by United), through the landmarked 1941 lobby (which is currently outside of security) and into the new concourse. The expansion would "deliver a modern passenger convenience while respecting the terminal's historic context," the MWAA planning documents state. They estimate a walking distance of 2,700 feet from check-in to the farthest gate (about the length of 7 1/2 football fields). The new space would even include 10,000 square feet for an as-yet-unnamed new airline lounge. Southwest executives have repeatedly teased plans to potentially invest in a lounge network. PGAL, the architecture firm for the E gates at DCA and the under-construction Concourse E at IAD, will design the new concourse. The banjo, as well as several other nonlandmarked additions to the historic 1941 terminal, would be demolished once the new concourse opens. Related reading:

item.title: 16 mistakes cruise ship passengers make on disembarkation day
item.description:
Source: The Points Guy Score: 5.00
16 mistakes cruise ship passengers make on disembarkation day You've had a great cruise, and you want to end your vacation on a high note. Then comes the reality of disembarkation day. Getting off a cruise ship is not the same as checking out of a hotel — you can't just leave the ship when you feel like it. Small and luxury ships can have flexible, even leisurely, disembarkation plans. However, the final day on most big ships is a bit chaotic. The crew needs to get everyone out of their cabins and off the ship quickly so they can prepare for the arrival of the next batch of thousands of passengers. It's a busy work day. So, extend your calm vacation mindset a little longer by preparing yourself and taking these steps to avoid common disembarkation-day mistakes. Check your bill The night before disembarkation, a statement of everything you spent on the ship for drinks, specialty restaurants, spa treatments, souvenirs and any other splurges will arrive outside your cabin door. Mistakes do happen, so there will inevitably be long lines at guest services on disembarkation day, with people discussing specific charges. Avoid the crowd by either getting there super early or, better yet, heading to guest services on the last night of your cruise and asking for a printout. Carefully check the statement, and ask for any required adjustments. On some ships, you can even do this electronically on the cruise line's app or smart TV. One line item you'll likely see on that statement is daily gratuities, which most cruise lines add automatically to cover standard service. If your room steward, waiter or another crew member went above and beyond, an extra cash tip on the last night is a nice — and appreciated — gesture, though it's not required. Pro tip: Don't assume you can fix billing issues after you get off the ship. It's nearly impossible to get cruise line land staff to fix onboard mistakes. Don't get up at the crack of dawn Your ship might arrive back in port at 6 a.m., but customs clearance might take two hours or more. Enjoy an extra hour or two of sleep — unless you still need to check your bill that morning. Avoid early flights home There is a reason cruise lines recommend guests don't book return flights before noon. It takes several hours to clear a ship of thousands of passengers. You might also have to clear customs. Then, you have to get to the airport, which could involve navigating through heavy traffic and waiting in security lines along with hundreds of other cruise travelers fresh off their ships. Avoid unnecessary heart palpitations by booking afternoon flights. Related: Should I book my flight through my cruise line? Check your luggage tags The day before disembarkation, staff will deliver color- and number-coded luggage tags to your cabin, along with an approximate disembarkation time. The idea is that you put these tags on any luggage you would like the crew to handle (more on this below). These tags are important for both departure timing and finding your suitcase at the pier. On disembarkation day, groups will be called by the tag color and number — such as Red 1 or Yellow 5 — to head to the atrium to disembark. Don't bother getting there early; you'll end up milling around, which can be frustrating. It's better to grab a coffee and wait in a lounge or out by the pool. Related: A beginners guide to picking a cruise line Don't forget your group color Luggage at the pier will be sorted by group color and number — and there will be thousands of bags waiting. Take a photo or otherwise note your tag color so you know where to look for your bags. Pack up your liquor purchases If you picked up a bottle of Kahlua in Mexico, rum in Jamaica or duty-free booze on your ship, the cruise line likely held it until the final night of the sailing. You must pick up your liquor at the time and place your cruise ship tells you before you disembark. (Alternatively, some cruise lines set up a table in the port building on debarkation morning.) Pack your bottles in checked baggage if you are flying home. Carefully wrap them in your dirty clothes. U.S. Customs and Border Protection allows you to enter the country with 1 liter of an alcoholic beverage per adult, duty-free. You can bring in more, but you'll have to pay the taxes on it. Put out your luggage The system for removing bags from the ship works this way: On the last night of your cruise, you pack your large bags and leave them in the hall for the crew to remove and transfer to the pier. You also have the option of carrying your own luggage off the ship, a process known as self-assist or express walk-off. It sometimes requires signing up in advance — either the night before via the ship's app or a form at guest services — in exchange for one of the earliest disembarkation times. However, this is only recommended if you are able-bodied and can haul your bags down flights of stairs on the ship and at the cruise terminal. Elevator banks on both will be extremely crowded. It's usually better to pack as much as you can in your luggage and let someone else do the heavy lifting. (An exception is if you only have a light carry-on, in which case, go for it.) Set aside clothes for the morning A rookie mistake is packing too much in the luggage that you leave outside the door, then waking up the next day to realize you forgot to leave out shoes, pants or other necessary items. Don't be the one walking to the pier barefoot or in your pajamas. You'll want to have a carry-on suitcase or tote set aside so you can bring your toothbrush, pajamas and other items off the ship. The last night is typically casual, and some cruisers find it easiest to wear the same clothes off the ship the next morning. Pro tip: If you have any items that can't go in the plane but you need at night, put them in a small separate bag so you remember to transfer them to your checked luggage before you get to the airport. Related: What to wear on a cruise: Cruise attire and cruise line dress codes Scour your cabin You will typically be asked to vacate your cabin by 9 a.m. or earlier on disembarkation day so that the crew can prepare for the next passengers. If you leave any items behind, it's difficult to recover them once you're off the ship. Do a careful check of closets, drawers and even under the bed to make sure you have packed everything. Don't forget the bedside table drawers, the very back of the shelves and the safe. If you are traveling with kids, also look for small stuffed animals or other toys hidden in any crumpled linens on the bed. Don't take the bathrobe If you are in a cabin that comes with a bathrobe and slippers, the slippers are typically yours to keep. However, you will be charged if you walk off with the bathrobe. The same rule applies to pool or beach towels stored in your cabin. Check your safe Given that safes are tucked away in closets, it's easy to forget about the important items — passports, wallets, jewelry — you've set inside. Check the safe first thing when you get up on disembarkation day, and make sure to reach into every corner to feel for any forgotten items. Don't pack your keycard, ID or passport You might think you are done with your keycard when you vacate your cabin, but you will need to tap it once more when you get off the ship. You'll need to show your passport or other official identification to customs officials at the cruise terminal. If you have received a customs form, it's important to fill it out (one per family) before you disembark. Related: Do I need a passport to cruise? Go to breakfast Room service is not always available on disembarkation day. Head to the buffet or main dining room to enjoy a leisurely breakfast — unless you're in a rush to get to your flight. Check the opening hours before you go, as breakfast venues will likely serve meals on a different schedule on the last day of the cruise. Respect cabin vacancy times You will frustrate your room stewards if you linger in your cabin beyond the recommended clear-out time. Remember that they only have a few hours to clean and set up every room on board for the next group of cruisers. Don't make their job more difficult by overstaying your welcome in your cabin. Leaving a packed carry-on bag in one corner, out of the way, while you go to breakfast might be acceptable. It doesn't hurt to ask. Related: How long does it take to disembark a cruise ship? Know what your luggage looks like When you get to the cruise terminal area where thousands of bags have been placed, it helps if you know exactly what your suitcases look like. Putting a colorful ribbon or string on your bags will help you spot them. Once you spot your bags, porters are often on hand to help load them onto a cart or into an Uber or cab. It's customary to tip $2 to $3 per bag for the help, and it's worth having small bills ready, especially if you're traveling with several suitcases or kids in tow. Don't run to the bus If you've paid your cruise line for an airport transfer, don't get stressed about missing the bus. There will be plenty available. Staff will be on hand to direct you to a bus to your specific airline and terminal, or to one that makes a circuit to several terminals at the airport. The buses will run again and again until everyone gets a lift. Planning a cruise?
